FR-011 Data Completeness Indicator
Input: Validated data set, rejected data entries, missing data entries, time range, location, and data type.
Output: Completeness indicator for query results, feeds, dashboards, and reports.
Description: The system must calculate and expose data completeness indicators showing the proportion or presence of rejected, missing, stale, or unavailable data within the relevant scope.
FR-012 Reduced-Confidence Indicator Propagation
Input: Reduced-confidence determination, degraded context output, affected outputs list, and quality status.
Output: Updated confidence indicators across views and published outputs.
Description: When data quality, completeness, staleness, or fallback conditions reduce confidence in an output, the system must propagate consistent reduced-confidence indicators to dashboards, historical queries, published feeds, MI Drive outputs, shared views, and reports.
2.3 Traffic Metrics Calculation
FR-013 Traffic Metrics Calculation
Input: Validated traffic data, probe vehicle data, sensor data, cached data, and archived travel time history.
Output: Congestion levels, travel times, queue lengths, and traffic performance indicators.
Description: The system must calculate key traffic performance indicators using predefined or configured algorithms.
FR-014 Metric Calculation Fallback When Algorithms Fail
Input: Algorithm availability, validated traffic data, last successful metric results, and archived or cached travel time history.
Output: Fallback congestion levels, fallback travel times, metric freshness indicator, and travel time completeness indicator.
Description: When configured calculation algorithms or scripts fail, the system must continue providing best-available traffic outputs using last successful metrics or cached and archived travel time history. Outputs produced this way must be marked with freshness and completeness indicators.
FR-015 Traffic Metrics Fallback on Validated Data Failure
Input: Traffic metrics calculation request, validated traffic data availability, and last complete validated dataset.
Output: Safe congestion levels, safe travel times, and metric confidence status.
Description: When current validated traffic data is unavailable, the system must use the last complete validated dataset where appropriate and explicitly communicate metric confidence status.
2.4 Incident Detection and Event Lifecycle Management
FR-016 Incident Detection and Classification
Input: Anomalies in traffic flow, sensor data, probe data, and road condition context.
Output: Incident reports with type, location, severity, time, and status.
Description: The system must detect potential incidents and classify them based on predefined rules or configured logic.
FR-017 Incident Classification Failure Recovery
Input: Incident type determination failure and undefined severity indicators.
Output: Default severity mapping and alert dispatch with degraded classification status.
Description: When an incident type or severity cannot be determined, the system must apply a predefined fallback severity mapping and clearly mark related alerts or outputs with degraded classification status.
FR-018 Event Lifecycle Management
Input: Event creation, modification, assignment, progress update, closure request, and requester identity.
Output: Updated event status, lifecycle history, and audit logs.
Description: The system must track the full lifecycle of each event from detection to resolution, including creation, assignment, progress, modification, closure, recovery, and completion logs.
FR-019 Authorization for Incident Event Modification and Closure
Input: Incident event modification request, closure request, requester identity, and user roles.
Output: Authorization decision and authorized action indicator.
Description: The system must restrict incident event modification and closure actions to authorized users. Unauthorized attempts must be rejected and logged.
FR-020 Event Status Recovery Propagation
Input: Recovered event status and affected event consumers.
Output: Updated event displays, updated report inputs, and recovery status.
Description: When an event status recovery occurs, corrected status outcomes must be propagated consistently to downstream consumers, including event displays, report inputs, and historical event records.
FR-021 Operational Notification for Event Audit Recovery
Input: Recovered event identifier and recovery result.
Output: Recovery notification record and recovery status.
Description: The system must notify operational stakeholders when event status or event audit recovery occurs and retain a durable notification record.
2.5 Road Surface and Weather Condition Inference
FR-022 Road Surface and Weather Condition Inference
Input: Weather station data, environmental sensor readings, road sensor data, and supporting traffic context.
Output: Road surface state, temperature, precipitation, and weather condition indicators.
Description: The system must infer current road surface and weather conditions using environmental data and supporting traffic context.
FR-023 Degraded Road and Weather Context Inference
Input: Weather station data, environmental sensor readings, and external traffic context availability.
Output: Road surface and weather outputs with reduced-confidence indicators.
Description: The system must provide best-available road and weather context outputs when external supporting context is unavailable, and must annotate degraded outputs with reduced-confidence indicators.
FR-024 Weather Inference Data Sufficiency Constraint
Input: Environmental sensor availability and inference confidence indicators.
Output: Inference completeness flags and alert suppression or downgrade decision.
Description: The system must enforce sufficiency thresholds before using road surface or weather inference outputs for weather-dependent alerting. If critical inputs are missing, dependent alerts must be suppressed, downgraded, or marked as incomplete.
FR-025 Road Surface Degradation Cascade
Input: Incident data failure, weather data failure, road surface derivation inputs, and inference results.
Output: Road surface degraded indicator and downstream eligibility status.
Description: When incident or weather inputs are unavailable or incomplete, the road surface state output must carry a degraded indicator and downstream eligibility status so consumers do not treat degraded outputs as fully reliable.
2.6 Dynamic Data Caching
FR-026 Dynamic Data Caching
Input: Processed data and recent frequently accessed data.
Output: Cached data accessible to internal and external applications.
Description: The system must maintain a dynamic cache of recent data for quick access by internal applications, external applications, dashboards, reports, and visualization services.
FR-027 Cache Freshness Expiration Constraint
Input: Cached data item and freshness window parameters.
Output: Cache validity decision and staleness indicator.
Description: The system must serve cached items only within their defined freshness window. Stale cache items must be refreshed, withheld, or served with an explicit staleness indicator according to configured policy.
FR-028 Cache Freshness Status Propagation
Input: Cache entry identifier and cache timestamp.
Output: Cache freshness status for the identified entry.
Description: The system must expose cache freshness status for each cached data entry and propagate that status to downstream consumers that read from the cache.
FR-029 Cache Update Failure State Exposure
Input: Cache update failure indicator and processed data inputs.
Output: Cache consistency status indicator.
Description: When cache updates fail, the system must expose a cache consistency status so downstream consumers can avoid using inconsistent cached data.
2.7 Long-Term Archiving and Historical Retrieval
FR-030 Long-Term Archiving
Input: Processed data, historical data, event data, metrics, weather data, and road condition data.
Output: Archived data stored in Oracle 10G for future analysis.
Description: The system must archive processed data in Oracle 10G for retrieval, historical analysis, compliance review, and reporting.
FR-031 Processed Data Archiving Failure Recovery
Input: Processed data, archiving job, failed processed data, event status transition, and audit log entry.
Output: Preserved failure state, retried archiving, no inconsistent archived data, and audit gap indicator where applicable.
Description: The system must prevent inconsistent long-term archival when processed data generation or archival jobs fail. Partial or failed archival states must be preserved, retried, and made visible to operators.
FR-032 Retention-Driven Archival Data Removal
Input: Retention policy outcome and archived data identifier.
Output: Removed or deactivated archived data and updated query visibility.
Description: The system must apply retention policies to archived data. Records beyond the retention period must be removed or deactivated, and historical query visibility must reflect retention-driven removal.
FR-033 Historical Data Query
Input: Time range, location, data type, user identity, and query criteria.
Output: Historical data records, visualization output, export output, or denied access response.
Description: The system must allow authorized users to query past traffic, weather, incident, event, and road condition data with visualization or export options.
FR-034 Authorization Control for Historical Queries
Input: User identity, query request, requested data scope, and role permissions.
Output: Authorized query results or authorization-denied status.
Description: The system must restrict access to historical query results based on user permissions. Authorization must be enforced at query execution time.
FR-035 Historical Data Query Fallback
Input: Historical data query, processed data availability, fallback dataset, and archive availability.
Output: Query results from the last complete archive and explicit query degradation status.
Description: When current processed data is unavailable, the system must provide best-available historical query results from the last complete archived dataset and clearly communicate degraded query status.
FR-036 Historical Retrieval Behavior for Missing Archived Records
Input: Query parameters and archival availability indicator.
Output: Retrieval outcome and partial-results indicator.
Description: When archived records are missing or unavailable for the requested range, the system must distinguish legitimate empty results from archive gaps and return a partial-results indicator where applicable.
FR-037 Audit Logging for Historical Data Access
Input: User identity, query criteria, query outcome, result summary, and timestamp.
Output: Historical data access audit record.
Description: The system must log historical data query activity for traceability, including user identity, query criteria, timestamp, outcome, and result summary or correlation key.
2.8 Data Publication and External Outputs
FR-038 Data Publication
Input: Processed data and target publication configuration.
Output: Published data in TMDD, SAE J2354, and other configured formats.
Description: The system must generate standardized output files and publish them to designated endpoints.
FR-039 Publication Endpoint Readiness Check
Input: Endpoint identifier for a downstream publication target.
Output: Endpoint readiness status and last known response.
Description: The system must check downstream publication endpoint readiness before and during publication. Unavailable or degraded endpoints must be used to gate, defer, or route publication attempts.
FR-040 Publication Failure Handling
Input: Processed data, publication target, output artifact identifier, and publication attempt outcome.
Output: Failed publication notice, publication status indicator, deferred publication queue status, and consistent output state.
Description: The system must handle publication failures by withholding partial outputs, preserving the last consistent published state, recording failure status, and placing affected outputs into a deferred queue where appropriate.
FR-041 Publication Availability and Consistency Recovery
Input: Processed data unavailability, failed processed data generation, partial publication attempt indicators, and last successfully published dataset.
Output: Published data from last-known valid snapshot, rollback status, publication status indicator, and publication audit trail.
Description: When processed data cannot be generated or publication fails, the system must revert to the last successfully published dataset where appropriate and prevent consumers from receiving partial or inconsistent outputs.
FR-042 Publication State Visibility
Input: Output type identifier and time window.
Output: Publication state, publication timestamps, endpoint identifiers, and failure state indicator.
Description: The system must expose publication state for generated outputs, including timestamps, endpoint identifiers, transient failures, and persistent unavailability.
FR-043 MI Drive Presentation Support
Input: Processed data, map overlays, incident data, road condition data, weather data, and fallback visualization dataset.
Output: Data formatted for MI Drive visualization tools.
Description: The system must provide compatible outputs for MDOT’s MI Drive system.
FR-044 MI Drive Presentation Fallback
Input: MI Drive visualization request, processed data availability, queried overlay availability, and fallback visualization dataset.
Output: Last complete MI Drive formatted output, last compatible overlay output, feed unavailability indicator, or overlay-absent indicator.
Description: When current MI Drive data or requested overlay data is unavailable, the system must provide the best available compatible output and explicitly indicate feed unavailability or missing overlay data.
2.9 Alert Generation and Delivery
FR-045 Alert Generation
Input: Incident data, weather event data, road condition data, alert thresholds, user-defined rules, and default rule set.
Output: Alerts sent via email, SMS, API, mobile channel, or web notification.
Description: The system must generate and deliver alerts based on incidents, weather events, road conditions, configured thresholds, and user-defined rules.
FR-046 Alert Rule Fallback and Audit
Input: User-defined rule availability, incident candidate data, default rule set, alert identifier, recipients, and delivery outcome.
Output: Alert generated using fallback classification, alert status, and audit record.
Description: If user-defined alert rules cannot be applied, the system must use a default rule set and mark the alert as generated under fallback conditions. All alert delivery attempts and outcomes must be recorded.
FR-047 Alert Delivery Failure Notification
Input: Alert delivery failure, notification channel, alert identifier, and delivery status.
Output: Failure notification, missing-alert status record, and correlation-ready delivery status.
Description: The system must notify subscribed stakeholders or operators when alert delivery cannot be completed, record missing-alert status, and link delivery outcomes to the originating alert.
FR-048 Mobile Alert Delivery Fallback
Input: Mobile alert delivery failure indicators and user contact preferences.
Output: Alternate-channel alert notification and user-visible delivery status.
Description: If mobile alert delivery fails, the system must attempt delivery through the next available configured channel and display or record the resulting delivery status.
FR-049 Alerting Degradation Notification
Input: Real-time traffic data availability status, alerting pipeline status, and recipient notification preferences.
Output: Operator notification and alerting status indicator.
Description: The system must notify relevant stakeholders when alert generation is degraded due to missing real-time traffic data or degraded classification quality.
FR-050 Alert Operation Authorization
Input: User identity, alert operation type, role, and permission profile.
Output: Allowed or denied decision for the requested alert operation.
Description: The system shall restrict alert creation, acknowledgement, suppression, deletion, and other protected alert operations based on assigned roles and permissions.
2.10 Web-Based User Interface and Dashboard
FR-051 Web-Based User Interface
Input: User queries, selections, filters, and visualization requests.
Output: Map display, incident icons, data overlays, dashboards, and data views.
Description: The system must provide a web-based UI with map-based views, icon layers, de-cluttering capabilities, data overlays, dashboards, and filtering options.
FR-052 UI Staleness Handling for Integrated Data Stream
Input: Integrated data stream availability, map display request, and data timestamp metadata.
Output: Suppressed stale overlays, staleness warning indicator, and last-known data expiry.
Description: The system must prevent stale integrated data from being presented as current. When data exceeds the staleness threshold, affected overlays must be suppressed or marked with staleness warnings.
FR-053 Map Display Fallback During Historical Query Degradation
Input: Map display request, historical data query degradation status, and degraded-history event record.
Output: Suppressed map layers, degraded-history status, and fallback to last complete snapshot.
Description: When historical query quality is degraded, affected map layers must be suppressed or served from the last complete snapshot with an explicit degraded-history status.
FR-054 Map Overlay Change Logging
Input: User identity, overlay configuration details, and timestamp.
Output: Map overlay change log record.
Description: The system must log user-driven map overlay configuration changes for traceability and audit review.
FR-055 Real-Time Dashboard
Input: Selected monitoring object, traffic data, weather data, event data, and dashboard configuration.
Output: Dynamically updated charts, metrics, indicators, and status panels.
Description: The system must provide a customizable real-time dashboard showing traffic flow, weather trends, event frequencies, and operational status.
FR-056 Degraded Real-Time Dashboard
Input: Dashboard request, external data source availability, and metrics confidence requirement.
Output: Suppressed indicators, insufficient-data status, and halted refresh for affected indicators.
Description: When external data is unavailable or below confidence requirements, the system must suppress affected dashboard indicators and display explicit insufficient-data status instead of presenting stale or fabricated data.
FR-057 Audit Logging for User-Facing Staleness Warnings
Input: User session and staleness warning display event.
Output: Staleness warning audit record and correlation key.
Description: The system must record user-facing staleness warning events and link them to the underlying data staleness condition.
2.11 Extensibility, Configuration, and Algorithms
FR-058 Extensibility and Configuration
Input: New data source definitions, algorithm configurations, output format configurations, and module definitions.
Output: Updated processing pipelines, configuration records, or output behavior.
Description: The system must allow configuration of new data sources, algorithms, and output formats without code changes where practical.
FR-059 Configuration Change Status Tracking
Input: Configuration change request and configuration scope.
Output: Configuration status values and status history.
Description: Each configuration change request must transition through defined status values such as pending, applied, failed, and rolled back. Status history must be retained for audit.
FR-060 Custom Algorithm Module
Input: User-submitted scripts, rule files, algorithm configuration, and authorization context.
Output: Results from custom processing logic or rejected algorithm update.
Description: The system must support configurable or custom algorithm modules for specialized traffic data analysis where authorized and validated.
FR-061 Authorization for Custom Algorithm Configuration Updates
Input: Algorithm configuration change request, requesting user identity, and target scope.
Output: Permitted update decision or denied update response.
Description: Only authorized users may update custom algorithm processing configurations. Authorization must be enforced across UI, API, and batch configuration imports.
FR-062 Rollback on Algorithm Update Failure
Input: Algorithm update identifier, application failure state, and last stable algorithm version.
Output: Stable prior algorithm usage and update failure indicator.
Description: When an algorithm update fails during application, the system must atomically roll back to the last stable algorithm version. Active computations must never use a partially applied algorithm state.
FR-063 Safe-State Handling for Algorithm Configuration Failure
Input: Algorithm configuration update failure indicators and prior configuration version.
Output: Last stable configuration, processing status indicators, and active configuration version.
Description: The system must revert to the most recently validated stable algorithm configuration when an update fails and expose the active configuration version and rollback reason.
2.12 User Access Control, Sharing, and Collaboration
FR-064 User Access Control
Input: User identity, role definition, permission profile, and requested resource.
Output: Controlled access permission, allowed action, or denied response.
Description: The system must implement Role-Based Access Control to ensure users only access authorized data, functions, views, APIs, and shared content.
FR-065 RBAC Role Assignment Management
Input: User identity, role selection, role assignment change request, and administrator identity.
Output: Role assignment result and updated access permissions.
Description: Authorized administrators must be able to create, modify, or revoke user role assignments. Role assignment changes must be persisted and applied to subsequent sessions.
FR-066 Authorization for Shared Content and Visualization Actions
Input: User identity, requested shared content, requested map visualization scope, and required permissions.
Output: Access granted or denied for shared content and map overlays.
Description: The system must evaluate every request to access shared content or map visualization overlays against user permissions before returning or rendering data.
FR-067 Data Sharing and Collaboration
Input: Shared links, shared reports, shared map views, shared alerts, user identity, and permission settings.
Output: Accessible shared content with permission control.
Description: The system must allow users to share specific map views, reports, or alerts internally or externally while enforcing access permissions.
2.13 Reporting and Analytics
FR-068 Automated Report Generation
Input: Report template, time range, geographic area, metrics, and report schedule.
Output: PDF, HTML, or configured report output containing key metrics.
Description: The system must support generating daily, weekly, monthly, scheduled, and on-demand reports with statistics such as average speed, congestion index, incident counts, weather summaries, and road condition trends.
FR-069 Automated Report Generation Error Handling
Input: Report request parameters and generation error conditions.
Output: Report generation failure outcome and structured error reason.
Description: When a report cannot be generated, the system must record the failure outcome with an error reason, notify the requesting user or scheduled job owner, and ensure no partial or corrupt report artifact is delivered or stored.
2.14 Multi-Language and Mobile Support
FR-070 Multi-Language Support
Input: Selected language and localization resources.
Output: Localized interface and message display.
Description: The system must support multiple languages and localized messages for user-facing content.
FR-071 Mobile-Friendly Interface
Input: Mobile device access request and user interaction.
Output: Responsive web interface optimized for smartphones and tablets.
Description: The system must provide a mobile-friendly interface for map browsing, dashboard viewing, alerts, and common user workflows.
2.15 Disaster Recovery and Reliability
FR-072 Disaster Recovery Mechanism
Input: System failure, disruption signal, failover trigger, and recovery configuration.
Output: Automatic failover to backup node and service restoration.
Description: The system must provide high availability and disaster recovery capabilities to ensure continuous operation during outages.
FR-073 Publication and Output Consistency Rollback
Input: Processed data generation failure, partial publication attempt, recovered validated inputs, and last consistent published outputs.
Output: Rollback to last consistent published outputs and degraded processing indicators.
Description: The system must preserve consistent output availability when processed outputs cannot be generated from current inputs. Rollback state and degraded indicators must be maintained atomically so consumers do not receive mixed or misleading outputs.
FR-074 Continuity Status Error Handling
Input: Fallback data selection failure, continuity status update attempt, and validation outcome.
Output: Correct continuity status indicator and error state indicator.
Description: When continuity status determination fails, the system must resolve the failure to a definitive error state and prevent downstream processing from proceeding with ambiguous continuity status.
FR-075 Audit Failure Notification and Degraded Alert Audit
Input: Audit log recording failure, event modification or closure actions, degraded incident classification status, alert dispatch event, and user contact preferences.
Output: Audit failure notification, alert audit log entry, and audit status indicator.
Description: The system must notify stakeholders when incident event changes cannot be reliably audited and must record traceable audit entries for alert generation events using degraded incident classification states.

Functional Requirements
3.1 User Management
3.1.1 User Registration
Description: User fills in registration details and the system saves them to the database. The system must validate uniqueness of user identifiers before creation.
Input: Username, Password, Email, PhoneNumber.
Output: New record inserted into the User table containing UserID, UserName, Password, Email, PhoneNumber, or a registration rejected result with conflict message.
3.1.2 User Login
Description: User enters the registered username and password; the system verifies the credentials. If authentication fails, the system must return a clear failure message without exposing protected account or payment data.
Input: Username, Password.
Output: If credentials are valid, login-success message and system access granted; otherwise, an error message prompting re-entry.
3.1.3 Manage User Information
Description: Administrator or the account owner updates personal data. The system must authorize the operation before applying any change.
Input: Requesting actor identifier, target UserID, updated fields.
Output: Updated record in the User table or an operation denied result.
3.1.4 Delete User
Description: Administrator or an authorized account owner permanently removes a user from the system. On deletion, dependent access to cart, order initiation, and stored payment methods must be safely revoked while retaining completed order records only as needed for audit purposes.
Input: Requesting actor identifier, target UserID.
Output: User record removed from the User table or a deletion denied result.
3.1.5 Authorize User Account Management
Description: The system must verify that the requesting actor has the required permission before allowing any create, read, update, or delete operation on a user account. Unauthorized requests must be denied and no changes applied.
Input: Requesting actor identifier, target UserID, requested operation.
Output: Allowed or denied operation result.
3.1.6 Enforce Unique User Identifiers at Registration
Description: The system must prevent creation of user accounts that violate uniqueness rules for Username or Email.
Input: Username, Email.
Output: Registration accepted or rejected result with conflict message.
3.1.7 Require Active Authenticated User for User-Scoped Operations
Description: Any operation referencing a UserID must be accepted only when it maps to an existing, non-deleted, currently authenticated user account.
Input: UserID, authentication state.
Output: Valid-user confirmation or invalid-user denial message.
3.2 Restaurant Browsing
3.2.1 Browse Restaurants
Description: User views the list of restaurants in the system.
Input: None.
Output: Restaurant list, each entry including RestaurantID and other relevant details.
3.2.2 Search Restaurants
Description: User searches for restaurants using keywords. If no results are found, the system must return a meaningful no-results response and allow the user to continue discovery.
Input: Search keyword.
Output: List of restaurants matching the keyword, or a no-results message with refinement guidance and browse-all option.
3.2.3 View Restaurant Details
Description: User views detailed information for a specific restaurant. If the RestaurantID is invalid, the system must return a descriptive not-found message rather than a blank or failed page.
Input: RestaurantID.
Output: Full details of the selected restaurant, or an error message indicating the restaurant was not found.
3.3 Shopping-Cart Management
3.3.1 Add Dish to Cart
Description: User adds a selected dish to their personal shopping cart. The system must verify that the acting user is authorized, the cart context exists, and the dish is valid and usable before insertion.
Input: UserID, DishID.
Output: New cart item inserted into ShoppingCart table containing ShoppingCartID and DishID, or a failure result with appropriate message.
3.3.2 Remove Dish from Cart
Description: User removes a dish from their shopping cart. The system must handle removal of non-existing items gracefully and keep dependent cart fields consistent.
Input: UserID, DishID.
Output: Selected dish record removed from ShoppingCart table, updated cart summary, or a not-found result with unchanged cart state.
3.3.3 Authorize Cart Operations
Description: Only the authenticated, authorized user who owns the cart may add or remove dishes in that cart. Unauthorized requests must be denied and no cart changes applied.
Input: User identity, UserID, DishID, requested cart operation.
Output: Allowed or denied action result.
3.3.4 Ensure Shopping Cart Context Exists Before Modification
Description: Before any cart modification, the system must verify that an active cart exists for the given UserID. If no cart context is found, the operation must be rejected with guidance to initialize or re-enter selection.
Input: UserID, DishID, requested cart operation.
Output: Cart modification accepted result, or cart-context-missing failure message.
3.3.5 Add Dish to Cart Transaction Rollback
Description: If adding a dish to the cart fails for any reason, all partial writes must be rolled back so the cart remains identical to its pre-operation state.
Input: UserID, DishID.
Output: Cart item not present confirmation and failure message.
3.3.6 Validate Cart Ownership and Non-Empty Contents Before Order Creation
Description: Before creating an order from a cart, the system must verify that the cart belongs to the requesting user and contains at least one purchasable item.
Input: UserID, cart identifier or cart items.
Output: Order creation accepted or validation failure result.
3.3.7 Update Dependent Cart State After Cart Item Removal
Description: When a dish is removed, the system must recalculate and persist dependent cart values such as total price, item count, and discounts atomically with the item removal.
Input: UserID, DishID.
Output: Updated cart summary result.
3.3.8 Handle Removal of Non-Existing Cart Item
Description: The system must return a clear not-found result when a removal is requested for a dish that is not currently in the user’s cart, leaving the cart unchanged.
Input: UserID, DishID.
Output: Removal accepted or not-found result.
3.4 Order Management
3.4.1 Create Order
Description: User generates an order from the shopping cart. The system must create the order only when validation succeeds and must establish corresponding order status information.
Input: UserID, Shopping Cart identifier, all DishIDs in the user’s cart.
Output: New order created in Order table with OrderID, UserID, OrderDate, and related status information.
3.4.2 Modify Order
Description: User edits an unfinished order. The system must authorize the request and apply changes only when the order is still editable.
Input: UserID, OrderID, updated list of DishIDs.
Output: Updated order record in Order table or denied result.
3.4.3 Cancel Order
Description: User cancels an unfinished order. The system must return the final cancellation outcome and apply downstream effects consistently.
Input: UserID, OrderID.
Output: Cancellation status result and updated order state.
3.4.4 Pay Order
Description: User completes payment for an unpaid and payable order using a valid payment method associated with that order and user.
Input: UserID, OrderID, payment-method details or reference, payment amount.
Output: New payment record inserted into PaymentRecord table with PaymentRecordID and amount, or payment rejected result.
3.4.5 View Order Status
Description: User checks the status of an order. The system must verify that the order exists and belongs to the requesting user before disclosing status information.
Input: UserID, OrderID.
Output: Displayed status information of the selected order, or a denial / not-found result.
3.4.6 Review Order
Description: User leaves a review for a completed order they are authorized to review. Invalid review attempts must be rejected without storing any partial review record.
Input: UserID, OrderID, rating, comment.
Output: New review record inserted into Review table with ReviewID, OrderID, UserID, etc., or a rejected submission result.
3.4.7 View Review Records for Eligible Orders
Description: Eligible users may view existing review records associated with a specific order only when they have a legitimate relationship to that order.
Input: OrderID, requester identity.
Output: Review list or review detail view result, or unauthorized result.
3.4.8 Order Operation Authorization
Description: Before modifying, cancelling, paying, viewing status, or reviewing an order, the system must verify that the requesting user is associated with the order and authorized for the requested operation.
Input: User identity, OrderID, requested operation.
Output: Allowed or denied operation result.
3.4.9 Require Valid and Payable Order for Payment
Description: The system must verify that the referenced OrderID exists, belongs to the requesting user, and is in a payable state before processing payment. Invalid, cancelled, already paid, pending-cancellation, or otherwise ineligible orders must not proceed to payment.
Input: UserID, OrderID, payment amount.
Output: Payment accepted or rejected result with explanatory message.
3.4.10 Validate Payment Method Before Payment
Description: Before processing a payment, the system must verify that the referenced payment method exists, belongs to the requesting user, is available for use, and is compatible with the referenced order.
Input: User identity, OrderID, payment-method reference or details.
Output: Payment eligibility result or missing / invalid method message.
3.4.11 Payment Atomicity and Consistency
Description: Payment processing and order status updates must remain consistent. If one step succeeds and a later step fails, the system must apply rollback or compensating logic so no inconsistent payment-record / order-status combination remains.
Input: User identity, OrderID, payment request details, payment processing result, order status update result.
Output: Deterministic final payment outcome and consistent post-operation state.
3.4.12 Rollback Create Order Failure
Description: If any step of the order creation flow fails, the system must roll back all partial writes so no incomplete order or order status record remains. The user’s cart state must be preserved as it was before the failed attempt.
Input: UserID, Shopping Cart identifier, DishIDs in the user’s cart.
Output: Order creation failure message and no new order record present.
3.4.13 Ensure Order Status Record Exists Before Downstream Processing
Description: If order status creation fails after the order record is created, the system must either roll back the order entirely or mark it as not processable and block payment initiation and further status advancement.
Input: OrderID, order creation result, order status creation result.
Output: Full rollback result or not-processable order state with downstream operations blocked.
3.4.14 Order State Change Confirmation
Description: After order creation, modification, cancellation, or payment, the system must provide explicit confirmation of the resulting order state, including status, timestamp, and relevant identifiers.
Input: User identity, OrderID, order action.
Output: Order state confirmation details.
3.4.15 Order State Change Failure Handling
Description: If an order state-changing operation fails mid-execution, the system must roll back any partial state change and keep the order in its last confirmed valid state. The user must receive a message showing the true final state.
Input: User identity, OrderID, order action.
Output: Failure outcome message and consistent post-failure order state.
3.4.16 Notify Order Cancellation Result
Description: Upon completion of a cancellation attempt, the system must inform the user whether the cancellation succeeded or failed and reflect the final state of the order.
Input: OrderID, cancellation result.
Output: Cancellation status message.
3.4.17 Notify Payment Completion Result
Description: After a payment attempt is processed, the system must deliver a clear success or failure message that reflects the actual transaction outcome.
Input: OrderID, payment outcome.
Output: Payment success or failure message.
3.4.18 Standardized Order Status Notifications
Description: Whenever an order transitions to a new status, the system must generate and deliver a consistent status update notification to the owning user.
Input: User identity, OrderID, new order status.
Output: Status update message.
3.4.19 Require Completed Order for Review Submission
Description: Review submission is allowed only for orders that have reached a completed status and are owned by the requesting user.
Input: UserID, OrderID, rating, comment.
Output: Review submission accepted or rejected result.
3.4.20 Handle Review Attempt With Invalid Order Context
Description: The system must reject review submissions for non-existent orders, orders not owned by the requesting user, or orders not eligible for review, and must not create any review record.
Input: UserID, OrderID, rating, comment.
Output: Review rejection or denial message with no review record created.
3.4.21 Define Cancellation Effects on Payment and Review Records
Description: Upon order cancellation, associated payment and review-related records must be handled according to defined business rules such as refund, void, invalidation, or eligibility revocation. All cascade effects must be applied atomically.
Input: OrderID.
Output: Cancellation impact result, payment handling outcome, and review eligibility or invalidation outcome.
3.4.22 Notify Affected Users About Cancellation Impact
Description: When an order cancellation changes payment or review eligibility, the system must notify affected users which order was cancelled, what actions are no longer available, and any next steps.
Input: OrderID, affected user identities.
Output: Notification delivery result.
3.4.23 Notify Review Stakeholders on Review Invalidation
Description: If an order state change invalidates existing review records or review eligibility, the system must notify affected stakeholders and update the displayed eligibility state.
Input: OrderID, review record identifier.
Output: Review invalidation notification outcome and updated review eligibility status.
3.5 Payment-Method Management
3.5.1 Manage Payment Methods
Description: User updates, creates, or deletes stored payment-method information. The system must preserve consistency and authorize the operation before applying changes.
Input: UserID, updated, created, or deleted payment-method details, requested operation.
Output: Updated, created, or removed record in the PaymentMethods table, or rejected result.
3.5.2 Rollback Payment Method Update or Deletion Failure
Description: If a payment-method update or deletion cannot be fully completed, the system must roll back all partial changes so the prior consistent state is preserved.
Input: UserID, payment-method operation, updated or deleted payment-method details.
Output: Operation failure result with rollback confirmation.
3.5.3 Handle Payment-Method Create or Update Exceptions Cleanly
Description: Payment-method creation and update operations must resolve to a clear success or failure outcome with no ambiguous or partial stored state.
Input: UserID, payment-method details, requested operation.
Output: Failure message or accepted result.
3.5.4 Preserve Stored Payment Methods on Management Failure
Description: If a payment-method management operation fails, all existing payment-method records must remain unchanged from their pre-operation state.
Input: UserID, updated or deleted payment-method details.
Output: Payment-method operation failure message and unchanged existing records.
3.5.5 Cascade Payment Eligibility Changes After Payment Method Update
Description: When a payment method is updated or deleted, the system must identify affected existing and future orders, update their payment eligibility accordingly, and explain impacted orders to the user.
Input: UserID, updated or deleted payment-method details.
Output: Affected payment eligibility outcome and user explanation.
3.5.6 View Payment Records
Description: User views all payment records related to them. Access must be restricted to the rightful authenticated user.
Input: UserID.
Output: List of payment records belonging to the user, or access denied message.
3.5.7 View Payment Record Details by Order
Description: User may view payment details associated with an order only when they own that order.
Input: UserID, OrderID.
Output: Payment record details for authorized user, or access denied message.
3.5.8 Payment Failure User Notification
Description: When payment fails, the system must return a human-readable failure message and clear next-step guidance, such as retrying, selecting another payment method, or contacting support.
Input: OrderID, User identity, payment failure condition.
Output: Payment failure message and next-step guidance.
3.5.9 Notify Payment Failure Reason Category
Description: The system must distinguish payment failure categories such as insufficient funds, card declined, unavailable payment method, or invalid method, and present the appropriate category with actionable guidance.
Input: OrderID, payment failure condition, payment method availability status.
Output: Failure reason category message and retry or update instructions.
3.5.10 Explain Recovery Expectations After Login Failure Blocking Payment Access
Description: When login failure prevents access to stored payment information, the system must provide recovery guidance such as password reset, account unlock, or support contact, while exposing no payment-method data.
Input: Username, Password.
Output: Login failure message, recovery expectations message, and no payment-method access.
3.6 System Administration and Audit
3.6.1 Create Order Status
Description: Administrator adds a new order status definition for use by the order workflow.
Input: Order-status description.
Output: New order-status record inserted into OrderStatus table with OrderStatusID and description.
3.6.2 Publish Review
Description: User publishes a new review only when review creation rules and authorization checks succeed.
Input: UserID, target-ID, review content.
Output: New review record inserted into the Review table, or rejected result.
3.6.3 Record Audit Logs for Account, Payment Method, Cart, Order, Review, and Administrative Changes
Description: Important state-changing actions across account management, shopping cart, order, payment-method, review, and administrative operations must produce immutable, queryable audit records.
Input: Actor identifier, affected record identifiers, change type, timestamp.
Output: Audit entry created result.
3.6.4 Log Denied and Sensitive Operations
Description: The system must log denied authorization attempts and other sensitive operations such as account deletion, payment-method changes, payment attempts, and review denials for compliance and incident investigation.
Input: Actor identifier, target resource, requested action, denial or outcome status, timestamp.
Output: Audit log entry.
3.6.5 Handle Operational Failures With Clear Error Outcomes
Description: Failures across user management, restaurant browsing, cart, order, payment-method, and administrative functions must return clear user-visible error messages and actionable retry or recovery guidance without exposing internal system details.
Input: Operation type, input fields, failure condition.
Output: Error message outcome and retry guidance outcome.

Functional Requirement
3.1  User Management
3.1.1  Register
Description: New users create an account in QuickEats. The system must validate required fields, email/mobile uniqueness, password validity, and create the account and user profile atomically. If confirmation is required, the account must not be usable for login until confirmation succeeds.
Input: Name, mobile number, email address, password.
Output: Account and profile stored in the system database with confirmation email or SMS sent, or registration rejected with validation errors.
3.1.2  Login
Description: Registered users sign in with their credentials. The system must reject invalid credentials, expired sessions, and unconfirmed accounts with clear responses.
Input: Email address and password.
Output: Successful login redirects the user to their personal homepage; failed login returns an authentication or account-status error.
3.1.3  Edit Personal Information
Description: Logged-in users can update their own profile. The system must verify that the logged-in user owns the target profile before applying updates.
Input: Login status, user identifier, target profile identifier, updated personal details.
Output: Updated profile saved in the database, or update denied with an authorization error.
3.1.4  View Order History
Description: Logged-in users view their own past orders. The system must deny the request if the session is absent, expired, or invalid.
Input: Login status, user identifier.
Output: List of the user’s orders with full details, or access denied response.
3.1.5  View Restaurant Information
Description: Users browse detailed restaurant pages.
Input: User navigation action or restaurant identifier.
Output: Restaurant details including address, rating, opening hours, menu information, and availability status.
3.1.6  Account Confirmation Recovery
Description: If account confirmation email or SMS cannot be delivered, the system must provide a resend option or alternate confirmation path with abuse prevention controls.
Input: User contact details, confirmation request, delivery failure status.
Output: Resend option, alternate confirmation status, or confirmation failure message.
3.1.7  User Account Deletion
Description: Users may request permanent account removal. The system must authenticate the requester, confirm deletion intent, and reject deletion when unresolved conditions such as pending orders or outstanding balances exist.
Input: Logged-in user identifier, account deletion request.
Output: Deletion accepted, scheduled deactivation/removal outcome, or rejection reason.
3.1.8  Authentication Requirement for User Actions
Description: User profile operations, order history viewing, review posting, and payment-related user actions must only occur after successful authentication. Denied requests must not expose profile, order, or payment data.
Input: User login status, requested user action type.
Output: Action allowed, or action denied with appropriate error response.
3.1.9  Notification Fallback for Profile and Payment Default Updates
Description: If the primary notification channel cannot deliver the outcome of a profile update or default payment method update, the system must make the result visible through an alternate method such as in-app status or update history.
Input: User identity, update request, notification delivery failure reason.
Output: Alternate result visibility method and user retry guidance.
3.2  Restaurant Administration
3.2.1  Add Dish
Description: Restaurant administrators add new dishes for ordering. The system must authorize the administrator before creating the dish.
Input: Admin login, dish details including name, price, image, and description.
Output: New dish stored and displayed on the restaurant menu, or operation denied.
3.2.2  Update Dish
Description: Restaurant administrators modify existing dishes. Dish updates must be atomic so partial updates such as image-only or price-only changes are not persisted if any step fails.
Input: Admin login, dish identifier, updated dish details.
Output: Updated dish saved and menu refreshed, or update rejected/rolled back.
3.2.3  Delete Dish
Description: Restaurant administrators remove dishes from the menu. When a dish is deleted, existing cart items referencing that dish must be removed or flagged, and new orders must not include the deleted dish.
Input: Admin login, selected dish identifier.
Output: Dish removed or marked unavailable, affected carts updated, and checkout behavior updated.
3.2.4  View Restaurant Orders
Description: Restaurant administrators view orders related to their restaurant only. The system must verify both authentication and restaurant-scope permission before returning order data.
Input: Admin login session, restaurant administration scope.
Output: List of authorized restaurant orders with full details, or permission-denied response.
3.2.5  Process Order
Description: Restaurant administrators confirm or reject orders. The system must validate the administrator’s permissions and apply order status changes atomically.
Input: Admin login, order identifier, accept/reject action.
Output: Order status updated and user notified, or operation rejected/rolled back.
3.2.6  Administrative Session Establishment
Description: Successful administrator authentication must create an authorized session associated with the administrator’s restaurant administration privileges. All subsequent restaurant administration actions must be gated on this session.
Input: Administrator login credentials, administrator account.
Output: Administrator login session state and authorization context.
3.2.7  Administrator Authentication and Permission Enforcement
Description: Restaurant administration operations, including dish management, order viewing, and order processing, must be denied when the administrator is unauthenticated or lacks required permissions.
Input: Admin session, administrator permissions, requested admin action, requested restaurant identifier.
Output: Action allowed or denied with no unauthorized data returned or modified.
3.2.8  Roll Back Order Processing When Confirmation Fails
Description: If an order accept/reject action cannot be fully committed or user notification fails at a required confirmation point, the system must restore the order to its prior consistent state or expose a clear failure status to the administrator.
Input: Order accept/reject action, order status, administrator processing attempt.
Output: Order status restored or confirmed, and notification failure status where applicable.
3.2.9  Audit Administrator Order Decisions
Description: Administrator order decisions must be logged for accountability and dispute resolution.
Input: Admin identity, order identifier, order decision, decision timestamp.
Output: Immutable audit entry recorded.
3.2.10  Audit Administrator Login Failures and Denied Access
Description: Failed administrator login attempts and denied order-viewing requests must be recorded with correlation information to support incident investigation.
Input: Administrator login failure context, requested restaurant identifier, denied access event.
Output: Immutable audit record with correlation identifier.
3.3  Shopping-Cart Operations
3.3.1  Add Dish to Cart
Description: Users add dishes to the cart before checkout. The system must verify login status, dish availability, and cart eligibility before storing the cart item.
Input: User login, dish selection.
Output: Dish stored in the shopping-cart table, or add-to-cart rejected with reason.
3.3.2  Remove Dish from Cart
Description: Users remove dishes from the cart. The system must update the cart consistently after removal.
Input: User login, selected dish.
Output: Corresponding record deleted or marked removed from the shopping-cart table, and updated cart state returned.
3.3.3  Create Order from Cart
Description: Users place orders from the cart. The system must validate cart contents, delivery address, payment method, and item availability before committing the order.
Input: User login, delivery address, payment method, cart state.
Output: New order record created and payment flow initiated, or order creation rejected with validation result.
3.3.4  Shopping Cart Operation Atomicity
Description: Cart operations including add, remove, update quantity, and cart-dependent checkout changes must be atomic. If an operation fails, the cart must be restored to its prior consistent state with no partial changes persisted.
Input: User login, dish selection, cart operation type, failure condition.
Output: Cart operation result status and confirmed cart contents after operation.
3.3.5  Recover Cart State When Dish Becomes Unavailable
Description: If a dish becomes unavailable after being added to the cart, the system must remove or flag the affected cart entry before order creation proceeds.
Input: Dish selection, dish availability status, shopping-cart record.
Output: Cart entry removal or flagging outcome and cart consistency confirmation.
3.3.6  Validate Cart State Before Order Creation
Description: The system must verify that all cart items are available, purchasable, and compatible with the selected delivery address and payment method before order creation.
Input: Cart state, delivery address, payment method, cart item availability.
Output: Order creation success or rejection with specific cart validation result.
3.3.7  Restore Cart Integrity When Order Creation Fails
Description: If checkout-to-order creation fails due to address validation, payment method validation, persistence failure, or any other checkout error, the system must restore the cart to its exact pre-attempt state and leave no partial order record.
Input: Delivery address, payment method, cart state, failing checkout context.
Output: Order creation prevented, cart state restored, and safe retry outcome.
3.3.8  Restore Cart Integrity When Cancellation or Dish Update Fails
Description: If order cancellation or dish-related update fails during a cart-related workflow, the cart must be restored to its previous consistent state and the failed operation must not be reflected in the cart.
Input: Cancellation or dish update operation context, cart state, order identifier, dish identifier.
Output: Restored cart contents and failed operation status.
3.3.9  Apply Dish Deletion Effects to Cart and Checkout
Description: When a dish is deleted, cart items referencing that dish must be removed or marked unavailable, and checkout must prevent new orders from including it. Already placed in-flight orders are not affected by menu deletion.
Input: Deleted dish identifier, existing cart references, order creation request.
Output: Affected cart items updated and checkout behavior adjusted.
3.4  Order Management
3.4.1  Cancel Order
Description: Users cancel orders only when the order is in a valid cancelable state. Successful cancellation sets the order status to cancelled and restores or updates cart-related state according to business rules.
Input: User login, order to cancel.
Output: Order status set to cancelled and cart state updated, or cancellation denied.
3.4.2  Pay Order
Description: Users pay for existing orders. The system must validate ownership, order state, payment method eligibility, and idempotency before processing payment.
Input: User login, payment method, order details.
Output: Payment processed, order status set to paid, and payment record updated, or payment rejected.
3.4.3  Set Default Payment Method
Description: Users set a default payment method only when the method is valid, active, operable, and eligible for future payments.
Input: User login, payment details.
Output: Default payment method saved, or rejected with explanatory error.
3.4.4  View Payment History
Description: Users review their payment history. Only authenticated users may access their own payment records.
Input: User login.
Output: List of payment records with full details.
3.4.5  Pay Order Failure Handling
Description: When payment cannot be completed, the order must remain unchanged or be reverted to its pre-payment state. No partial paid state may be visible, and retries must not create duplicate charges.
Input: User login, payment method, order details, payment failure reason.
Output: Payment failure result status, order status unchanged or reverted, and payment consistency confirmation.
3.4.6  Payment Record Creation and Status Update
Description: The system must create or update payment records for payment attempts in a consistent and idempotent manner. Payment records must capture attempt timestamp, method, result, and failure reason where applicable.
Input: Order identifier, payment method, payment attempt details, payment outcome.
Output: Payment record creation or update outcome.
3.4.7  Payment Failure Recovery for Existing Orders
Description: On payment failure, the system must set the order payment status to a well-defined non-ambiguous value, update the payment record where applicable, and prevent duplicate charges through idempotency keys.
Input: Order details, payment method, payment failure state.
Output: Payment record update outcome and order payment status outcome.
3.4.8  Alternative Payment Method Selection After Payment Failure
Description: When a payment attempt fails, the system must allow the user to select an eligible alternative payment method and retry payment without rebuilding the cart or re-entering order details.
Input: Order identifier, payment failure state, alternative payment method candidates.
Output: Alternative payment eligibility outcome and payment retry permission outcome.
3.4.9  No Eligible Alternative Payment Handling
Description: If no eligible alternative payment method exists after a failed payment, the system must update the order payment status and provide clear next-step guidance.
Input: Order identifier, payment failure state, alternative payment method candidates.
Output: No-eligible-alternative outcome and order payment status details.
3.4.10  Terminal Payment Failure Outcome
Description: If alternative payment attempts fail or the recovery window expires, the system must mark the order payment status as terminally failed and ensure no partial or ambiguous state remains.
Input: Order identifier, payment failure state, alternative payment method selection result.
Output: Terminal payment failure outcome and user next-step guidance.
3.4.11  Payment Outcome Notification
Description: Users must be informed of final payment outcomes. Notifications must be issued only for terminal states and must include the order identifier and outcome.
Input: Order identifier, payment outcome, payment state indicator, user contact data.
Output: Success or failure notification delivered, queued, or made visible through an alternate in-app channel.
3.4.12  Payment Outcome Notification Retry
Description: If payment outcome notification delivery fails, the system must retry delivery and record failure if retries are exhausted. The outcome must remain visible through an alternate channel such as order status page or notification inbox.
Input: Payment outcome, user contact information, order identifier, notification delivery failure.
Output: Notification retry status and alternate outcome visibility.
3.4.13  User Outcome Notification for Payment and Cancellation
Description: The system must deliver a user-visible outcome message for terminal payment and cancellation results. Notification delivery status must be recorded so undelivered notifications can be retried.
Input: User login, order identifier, payment or cancellation action result.
Output: User-visible outcome message and notification delivery status.
3.4.14  Cancel Order Failure Recovery and Atomicity
Description: If cancellation fails partway through, order status and cart state must be restored to their pre-cancellation values. Cancellation must either fully succeed or leave all affected data unchanged.
Input: User login, order to cancel, cancellation failure state.
Output: Cancellation result status, unchanged/restored order status, and unchanged/restored cart state.
3.4.15  Cancel Order Eligibility Constraint
Description: Cancellation must be allowed only when the order is in a stable cancelable state, such as pending or unpaid. Paid, delivered, dispatched, previously cancelled, or transitional orders must be rejected.
Input: User login, order identifier, current order status.
Output: Cancellation eligibility result and acceptance or rejection outcome.
3.4.16  Enforce Allowed Order Status Transitions
Description: The system must maintain explicit order status transition rules for create, pay, cancel, accept, reject, and completion actions. Invalid transitions must be rejected before data modification.
Input: Current order status, requested action.
Output: Transition executed or denied with explanatory error.
3.4.17  Revalidate Dish Availability at Order Confirmation
Description: Before payment processing begins, the system must re-check every cart item against current restaurant inventory and operating status. If any item is unavailable, the order must be rejected and the user must be informed.
Input: User, cart state, selected delivery address, payment method, cart item availability.
Output: Revalidation success outcome or order rejection outcome.
3.4.18  Notify Order Rejection Due to Dish Unavailability
Description: When order confirmation fails because dish availability cannot be confirmed, the system must notify the user which dishes are unavailable and provide next-step guidance.
Input: User, order identifier, dish availability revalidation result.
Output: Unavailability rejection message and order status details.
3.4.19  Recover Order Status Visibility After Payment Failure
Description: Payment failure must not cause administrators or users to see the order as paid. Order status views must use authoritative payment outcome data rather than cached or optimistic state.
Input: Order identifier, payment failure outcome, order view request.
Output: Correct unpaid status shown and no paid-state details disclosed.
3.4.20  Reconcile Payment Outcome Propagation Failure
Description: If payment outcome updates fail to propagate to order status views, the system must reconcile the order record using the authoritative payment outcome. If reconciliation cannot complete, the order must be flagged for review and stale status must not be displayed.
Input: Order identifier, payment outcome, administrator order view request.
Output: Consistent paid/unpaid visibility or error/manual-review status.
3.4.21  Audit Order Cancellation Actions
Description: Each cancellation attempt, successful or rejected, must produce an immutable audit entry for traceability.
Input: User, order identifier, cancellation outcome.
Output: Cancellation audit entry.
3.5  Review Management
3.5.1  Post Review
Description: Users publish reviews for restaurants or dishes only when they are authenticated, associated with the relevant completed order, and eligible to review the target entity.
Input: User login, order details, target restaurant or dish, rating, comment.
Output: Review saved and restaurant or dish ratings updated, or review rejected.
3.5.2  Manage Reviews
Description: Backend administrators moderate reviews by hiding, deleting, flagging, or restoring inappropriate or malicious content. Only authorized administrators may perform moderation actions.
Input: Admin login, moderation action type, target review identifier.
Output: Updated review list with adjusted visibility and ratings, or moderation denied.
3.5.3  Review Posting Eligibility
Description: Reviews may be posted only for completed and eligible orders. Users without a qualifying completed order containing the target restaurant or dish must be rejected. Each completed order may grant at most one review per reviewable entity.
Input: Logged-in user identifier, target restaurant or dish, order identifier.
Output: Review posting permission outcome.
3.5.4  Valid Account State for Review Posting
Description: Review posting must be denied when the user account is suspended, deactivated, or otherwise invalid.
Input: Logged-in user identifier, account status, order identifier.
Output: Review posting denied outcome and denial reason.
3.5.5  Review Rejection Feedback
Description: When review submission is rejected because the order is incomplete, cancelled, ineligible, or not associated with the user, the system must return a clear user-facing explanation without exposing sensitive internal details.
Input: Selected order identifier, order completion status, user identity.
Output: Review submission rejected response with explanation.
3.5.6  Review Removal
Description: Eligible users may remove a previously submitted review. The system must verify that the requester is the original author or an administrator before accepting removal.
Input: Review identifier, requesting user identifier.
Output: Review removal accepted or rejected outcome.
3.5.7  Maintain Rating Aggregates After Review Submission
Description: After each review submission, the system must recalculate and persist the aggregate rating for the affected restaurant or dish atomically with the review write.
Input: Order identifier, target restaurant or dish, review value.
Output: Updated rating aggregates.
3.5.8  Rating Aggregate Update After Review Moderation
Description: When a review is hidden, deleted, restored, or otherwise moderated, the system must recalculate the aggregate rating using only reviews visible to users.
Input: Restaurant or dish identifier, affected review identifier.
Output: Rating aggregate update status and recalculation confirmation.
3.5.9  Recover Review and Rating Aggregate Update Failures
Description: If review posting cannot be reconciled with rating aggregate updates, the system must roll back the review or hide it until consistency is restored. Review visibility and aggregate rating must not diverge.
Input: Review submission data, target restaurant or dish, aggregate update failure point.
Output: Review rollback outcome, review visibility consistency outcome, and consistent review/rating state.
3.5.10  Resolve Rating Consistency When Review Rollback Fails
Description: If review rollback cannot fully reconcile aggregate rating state, the system must apply compensating recalculation or flag the aggregate for correction while preventing orphaned review data from affecting user-facing ratings.
Input: Posted review rollback outcome, aggregate update failure point, target restaurant or dish.
Output: Rating consistency resolution outcome and user-facing review visibility outcome.
3.5.11  Authorization for Review Moderation Actions
Description: Only authorized administrators may perform review moderation actions. Unauthorized attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Administrator login status, moderation action type, target review identifier.
Output: Moderation permission check result and allowed/denied outcome.
3.6  System Administration
3.6.1  View All Orders
Description: System administrators view order records across the platform only after successful authentication and authorization.
Input: Admin login session and permissions.
Output: Display of all authorized orders with full details.
3.6.2  Add Administrator
Description: Super administrators create new administrator accounts and assign permissions.
Input: Super-admin login, new administrator details, assigned permissions.
Output: New administrator account stored with assigned permissions.
3.6.3  Manage Administrators
Description: Super administrators edit existing administrator accounts or delete inactive ones. Changes must be applied consistently to database records and permission status.
Input: Super-admin login, administrator account details to edit or delete.
Output: Updated or removed administrator account with corresponding database and system status changes.
3.6.4  Reject Administrative Actions on Failed Login
Description: Administrative operations attempted under unauthenticated, expired, or failed-login sessions must be rejected and must not produce partial administrative side effects.
Input: Email address, password, administrator login attempt, requested administrative action.
Output: Login failure response and denied action outcome.
3.6.5  Gate Administrator Order Viewing
Description: Administrator order viewing must require both a valid session and explicit permission for the requested platform or restaurant scope. Partial order result sets must not be returned on failed authentication or authorization.
Input: Admin login session, administrator permissions, order view request, requested restaurant identifier.
Output: Order list delivered or denied without leaking order details.
3.6.6  Audit Denied Administrative Access
Description: Denied administrative access events, including failed login, denied order viewing, and denied moderation actions, must be logged for investigation and compliance.
Input: Administrator identity or login context, requested resource, denied action, timestamp.
Output: Immutable audit record.
3.6.7  Audit Denied User Actions
Description: Denied profile actions caused by missing or failed authentication must be logged with user identity or anonymous marker, action type, and timestamp.
Input: User login failure context, requested user action type.
Output: Recorded denied action event.
3.6.8  Consistent User-Facing Error Outcomes
Description: User-facing failures in registration, login, profile update, cart operations, order creation, payment, cancellation, review submission, and administration must return clear messages and avoid exposing internal system details.
Input: Operation type, failure condition, affected record identifier where applicable.
Output: Clear error response and next-step guidance where appropriate.

Functional Requirement
Function Requirement 1: Register User
Input: Username, password, contact details.
Output: Registration success message or validation error message.
Description: System provides a registration form. The system validates required fields, identifier uniqueness, password rules, and contact details before saving the user account. If any registration step fails, all partial writes must be rolled back so no incomplete user account remains.
Function Requirement 2: View User Profile
Input: User identity or administrator target user identity.
Output: User profile details or user-not-found error.
Description: Users may view their own profile, and authorized administrators may view user profiles within their permission scope. Sensitive fields such as passwords, password hashes, and payment tokens must never be returned.
Function Requirement 3: Update User Profile
Input: User identity, updated contact details or profile information.
Output: Update success message or validation error message.
Description: Users may update their own registration and profile details. The system validates updated data using the same rules as registration, rejects duplicate email or phone values, and saves valid changes.
Function Requirement 4: Delete User
Input: Administrator identity, target user account.
Output: Deletion success message, deletion denied message, or deletion failure message.
Description: Authorized administrators may delete user accounts. Before deletion, the system verifies administrator privileges and checks whether the user has outstanding orders or other blocking dependencies. If deletion is denied or fails, the user account must remain unchanged and the requester must receive a clear reason.
Function Requirement 5: Add Restaurant
Input: Administrator identity, restaurant name, address, opening hours, and other required restaurant details.
Output: Restaurant creation success message or validation error message.
Description: Authorized administrators add new restaurants. The system validates required fields and creates the restaurant record only when all validation succeeds. Successfully created restaurants may be activated for downstream dish and order operations.
Function Requirement 6: Manage Restaurant
Input: Administrator identity, target restaurant, updated restaurant details.
Output: Update success message or validation error message.
Description: Authorized administrators edit restaurant information such as address, operating status, and opening hours. The system must use the latest persisted restaurant record before applying updates and reject operations based on stale data.
Function Requirement 7: Delete Restaurant
Input: Administrator identity, target restaurant.
Output: Deletion success message, deletion blocked message, restaurant-not-found message, or dependency list.
Description: Authorized administrators delete restaurants only when deletion is safe. Before deletion, the system verifies that the restaurant exists and checks for unfinished orders, associated dishes, and affected cart items. If dependencies exist, deletion must be blocked and the blocking dependencies must be reported.
Function Requirement 8: Add Dish
Input: Restaurant administrator identity, restaurant identifier, dish name, price, image, description, stock, and availability details.
Output: Dish creation success message or validation error message.
Description: Authorized restaurant administrators add dishes to a restaurant menu. The system validates dish data, including price, stock, and restaurant association, before saving the dish.
Function Requirement 9: Modify Dish
Input: Restaurant administrator identity, dish identifier, updated dish details.
Output: Dish update success message or validation error message.
Description: Authorized restaurant administrators modify dish information such as price, description, image, stock, and availability. The system validates updates and prevents partial or inconsistent dish records from being saved.
Function Requirement 10: Delete Dish
Input: Restaurant administrator identity, target dish.
Output: Dish deletion success message or deletion blocked message.
Description: Authorized restaurant administrators delete or disable dishes. Before deletion, the system checks pending orders and active cart references. If deletion would affect active carts, the system must either block deletion with a clear reason or consistently remove or flag the dish in affected carts according to configured policy.
Function Requirement 11: View Dish Details
Input: Dish identifier.
Output: Dish details including image, price, description, availability, and stock status, or dish-not-found error.
Description: Users view full dish information. If the dish reference is invalid, deleted, or unavailable for viewing, the system returns a standardized dish-not-found or unavailable response.
Function Requirement 12: Add to Cart
Input: User identity, dish identifier, requested quantity.
Output: Add-to-cart success message or specific error message.
Description: Users add dishes to their cart. The system verifies that the user is authorized, the dish exists, the dish is available, the requested quantity does not exceed stock, and the dish details are current before updating the cart. If the operation fails, the cart must remain unchanged.
Function Requirement 13: Remove from Cart
Input: User identity, dish identifier.
Output: Remove success message, updated cart state, or item-not-found message.
Description: Users remove dishes from their cart. The system updates the cart item list and recalculates totals atomically. If the dish has become invalid or unavailable, removal must still be allowed so the user can clean up the cart.
Function Requirement 14: Manage Cart
Input: User identity, cart action, dish identifier, quantity, or clear-cart command.
Output: Cart update success message, updated cart contents, or validation error message.
Description: Users manage cart contents in real time, including viewing the cart, adjusting quantities, and clearing the cart. The system validates ownership, quantity rules, dish availability, and cart consistency before applying updates.
Function Requirement 15: View Cart Contents
Input: User identity.
Output: Cart item list with quantities, prices, totals, or empty-cart result.
Description: Users view current cart contents. The cart view must reflect the latest item availability, pricing, deleted dishes, and quantity changes.
Function Requirement 16: Refresh Cart After Restaurant or Dish Changes
Input: Restaurant update, dish update, dish deletion, affected user carts.
Output: Cart update outcome or cart context error message.
Description: When restaurant or dish information changes, the system must update affected carts by recalculating totals, removing invalid items, or flagging unavailable items so users are warned before checkout.
Function Requirement 17: Create Order
Input: User identity, cart contents, selected restaurant, delivery address, payment method.
Output: Order creation success message or cart/order validation error message.
Description: Users create orders from their cart. Before order creation, the system verifies that the user account is active, the cart is non-empty, all items are available and purchasable, all items belong to the target restaurant, and the delivery and payment information are valid.
Function Requirement 18: Convert Cart to Order Safely
Input: User identity, cart contents, selected restaurant.
Output: Created order or order creation failure message.
Description: The system must snapshot cart items, quantities, and current dish prices atomically at the moment of order creation. If the cart state cannot be reliably captured or if totals differ from recomputed values, the system must notify the user and block or re-confirm order creation.
Function Requirement 19: Prevent Order Creation from Invalid Cart
Input: User cart, order creation request.
Output: Order creation blocked message and cart validation error.
Description: The system blocks order creation when cart contents are empty, inconsistent, unavailable, cross-restaurant, or reference invalid dishes. The user must receive a specific validation error identifying the issue.
Function Requirement 20: View Order
