Description: Customers may request re-sending of order confirmation emails from their order history when supported. The system must verify that the order belongs to the requesting customer and that a valid order identifier exists before sending. Email dispatch results must be recorded.
Input: Customer identity, order identifier, resend request.
Output: Re-sent confirmation email or failure response, email dispatch log.
1.28 Product Inventory Management
Description: Authorized administrators can add, update, or delete products in inventory. Inventory changes must be reflected in product browsing, search results, cart validation, and checkout readiness. Unauthorized inventory change attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Administrator identity, product details, inventory change action.
Output: Updated inventory database, refreshed product list, authorization denial when applicable.
1.29 Product Information Management
Description: Authorized administrators can update product information such as name, price, description, and category. The system validates and stores changes, updates browsing and search surfaces, and rejects unauthorized attempts without side effects.
Input: Administrator identity, product ID, updated product fields.
Output: Updated product information, refreshed product display, access denied response when applicable.
1.30 Product Categorization Management
Description: Authorized administrators can create, update, or delete product categories and assign products to categories. Category changes must be reflected in product listings and filtering options. Unauthorized category management attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Administrator identity, product ID, category ID or category name, category operation.
Output: Updated category assignment, updated category filters, authorization audit record.
1.31 Product Catalog Lifecycle Management
Description: Authorized administrators can create new product records and remove existing product records from the catalog. New products with valid attributes must become available in catalog and inventory views. Removed products must no longer appear as available for browsing or checkout.
Input: Administrator identity, product attributes, product identifier.
Output: Product record created or removed, updated catalog and inventory surfaces.
1.32 Administrator Login
Description: An administrator can log in using registered credentials. The system authenticates credentials, verifies that the administrator has the required role or permission for dashboard access, and creates an administrator session only after successful authentication. Failed authentication must not create any session or token.
Input: Administrator email, password, role information.
Output: Active administrator session, dashboard access, access denied response.
1.33 Administrator Logout
Description: A logged-in administrator can end their session by selecting the logout option. The system terminates the session and redirects the administrator to the login page or home page.
Input: Administrator logout request.
Output: Administrator session termination, redirection to login page or home page.
1.34 Administrator Authorization for Protected Actions
Description: Every protected administrative action must be checked against the administrator's active session, identity, role, and permissions before execution. This applies to product management, inventory management, category management, order management, payment configuration, notification configuration, and administrator account management. Unauthorized requests must be denied, logged, and must not produce side effects.
Input: Administrator identity, administrator session, requested administrative action.
Output: Action allowed or denied, authorization audit record.
1.35 Administrator Account Management
Description: Administrators can update their own account information, such as email, password, and profile details, where permitted. Administrative account updates must be validated and must not leave the account in a partially updated state. If an administrator account update fails, dependent administrative actions that require a stable account state must be denied until the account state is resolved.
Input: Administrator ID, updated account details, administrator session.
Output: Updated administrator account, failure message, blocked dependent action when applicable.
1.36 Order Information Management
Description: Authorized administrators can view and manage order information, including status updates, shipping address corrections, order cancellation, and permitted payment-related fields. All order management actions must require authorization, must not expose sensitive order data to unauthorized users, and must be reflected in order history and order status surfaces.
Input: Administrator identity, order ID, order management action, updated order fields.
Output: Updated order record, customer notification when applicable, access denied response.
1.37 Payment Processing
Description: The system processes customer payment during checkout, validates payment details, verifies transaction results, and updates order state only according to the actual payment outcome. Orders must not be marked confirmed when payment fails or remains unconfirmed. Inventory should be deducted only after payment and checkout confirmation rules are satisfied.
Input: Payment details, order details, customer session.
Output: Processed payment, payment failure response, updated order status, inventory update when appropriate.
1.38 Payment Detail Validation
Description: Payment details must be validated before payment is attempted. Invalid payment fields must halt checkout and return structured error messages identifying the invalid fields. Customers must receive guidance to correct payment details and retry. Checkout must not proceed to order confirmation until payment validation passes.
Input: Payment method details, validation errors.
Output: Payment detail acceptance or rejection, retry guidance, checkout blocked outcome.
1.39 Payment Failure Handling
Description: When payment fails during checkout, the system must set the order status to payment failed or another appropriate non-confirmed state, must not send an order confirmation email, must not deduct inventory, and must not update stored customer payment methods or eligibility indicators based on the failed attempt. The customer must receive a clear payment failure notification with retry guidance.
Input: Payment failure event, checkout request, customer notification preferences.
Output: Payment failed order state, no confirmation email, preserved account state, payment failure notification.
1.40 Payment Failure Rollback and Reconciliation
Description: If payment failure occurs after partial checkout state has been created, the system must roll back inventory reservations, payment intents, and partial order state where possible. If rollback cannot be completed, the rollback failure must be recorded and the order state must reflect the inconsistency for operator reconciliation instead of silently diverging inventory and order records.
Input: Payment failure event, inventory reservation, rollback result.
Output: Rolled-back checkout state, rollback failure status, consistent order state for reconciliation.
1.41 Payment Method Management
Description: Customers can add, edit, or remove stored payment methods. The system validates payment method details, securely stores valid methods, and removes deleted methods from checkout eligibility immediately. Invalid or unavailable payment methods must not be usable during checkout.
Input: Customer identity, payment method details, payment method identifier, add/edit/remove request.
Output: Updated list of payment methods, confirmation message, payment method validation failure.
1.42 Payment Configuration Failure Handling
Description: If payment configuration is missing, invalid, or unavailable, checkout must be blocked before payment submission. The system must clearly indicate the configuration issue and disable repeated payment attempts until the issue is resolved. Once payment configuration becomes valid, checkout eligibility should be re-evaluated.
Input: Payment configuration status, checkout request, retry request.
Output: Payment configuration failure status, disabled payment submission, restored checkout eligibility when resolved.
1.43 Customer Eligibility Consistency After Payment Failure
Description: Customer-level eligibility indicators, such as loyalty status, purchase thresholds, or promotion eligibility, must not be updated based on failed payment attempts. Eligibility recalculation may occur only after successful confirmed payments. Failed payment attempts must be recorded for audit or troubleshooting.
Input: Payment failure event, customer eligibility indicators.
Output: Eligibility indicators unchanged, payment failure recorded.
1.44 Email Notification Preferences
Description: Customers can configure email notification preferences for order updates, promotions, inventory alerts, and confirmation-related communications where applicable. The system validates the email address and stores the preference settings. Notification sending must follow the customer's configured preferences unless a mandatory transactional notification is required by policy.
Input: Customer identity, notification preferences, email address.
Output: Updated notification settings, confirmation of preference update.
1.45 Email Confirmation Sending
Description: The system sends confirmation emails for actions such as account registration, order placement, notification setup, and order confirmation resend. Each email dispatch attempt must produce a traceable record containing event type, recipient, timestamp, and send result. If sending fails, the customer must be informed and offered retry or recovery guidance where applicable.
Input: Customer email address, confirmation action, send result.
Output: Confirmation email sent, email failure message, email dispatch audit record.
1.46 Notification Delivery Failure Handling
Description: When a required customer notification cannot be delivered, such as payment failure or order confirmation communication, the system must record the delivery failure and update the user-facing notification state. Customers and administrators must not be shown a misleading successful delivery state when notification delivery failed.
Input: Notification request, delivery failure, related order or payment event.
Output: Notification delivery status recorded, user-facing notification outcome updated.
1.47 Order Confirmation Email Preference and Delivery Status
Description: Order confirmation email dispatch must respect applicable customer notification preferences while preserving transactional consistency. When an order confirmation email is sent, the result must be recorded. If delivery is disabled or fails, the system must update the confirmation communication status accordingly and provide customer guidance where needed.
Input: Order confirmation status, email notification preferences, email confirmation request.
Output: Confirmation email sent, suppressed, failed, or pending status.
1.48 Manage Payment Configuration
Description: Authorized administrators can manage system-level payment configuration where required. Unauthorized users must not be able to modify payment configuration. Changes must be validated, logged, and reflected in checkout payment method availability.
Input: Administrator identity, payment configuration change request.
Output: Payment configuration updated or denied, audit record.
1.49 Manage Email Notification Configuration
Description: Authorized administrators can manage system-level email notification configuration where required. Unauthorized configuration attempts must be denied and logged. Changes must not override customer-specific preferences unless explicitly required by system policy.
Input: Administrator identity, notification setup change request.
Output: Notification configuration updated or denied, audit record.
1.50 Manage Administrator Information
Description: Authorized administrators can manage permitted administrator account information. Changes to administrator account state, credentials, or roles must be validated and logged. Failed updates must return clear feedback and must not leave partial administrative account state.
Input: Administrator identity, administrator account update fields.
Output: Updated administrator information, failure feedback, audit record.
1.51 Order Confirmation State Transition Rules
Description: The system must enforce valid order confirmation state transitions. An order cannot transition to confirmed if payment failed, and a confirmed order cannot revert to pending without an explicit cancellation, refund, or correction flow. Invalid transition attempts must be rejected and the existing order state preserved.
Input: Payment processing outcome, current order state, requested confirmation state update.
Output: Valid state transition applied, invalid transition rejected.
1.52 Inventory Availability Consistency
Description: Product availability shown during browsing, search, cart review, and checkout must remain consistent with current inventory. Checkout submission must revalidate cart contents against inventory before payment begins. If any item becomes unavailable or quantity drops below the desired amount, checkout must be blocked and the customer must be informed of the affected items.
Input: Product availability display request, cart contents, current inventory levels, checkout attempt.
Output: Consistent availability outcome, checkout blocked when inventory is no longer valid.
1.53 Inventory Update Authorization and Audit
Description: Inventory changes may be performed only by authorized administrators. Every inventory update request must be validated against the administrator's identity and permissions. Both permitted and denied attempts should be auditable.
Input: Administrator identity, inventory change request.
Output: Inventory update permitted or denied, audit record.
1.54 Product Update Authorization and Audit
Description: Product information changes may be performed only by authorized administrators. Every product update request must be validated before execution. Unauthorized requests must be denied, logged, and must not alter product data.
Input: Administrator identity, product update request.
Output: Product update permitted or denied, audit record.
1.55 Category Management Authorization and Audit
Description: Category creation, update, deletion, and assignment may be performed only by authorized administrators. Unauthorized category management attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Administrator identity, category operation request.
Output: Category operation permitted or denied, audit record.
1.56 Order Management Authorization and Audit
Description: Order management actions may be performed only by authorized administrators or customers acting on their own orders. The system must verify actor identity, role, and scope before allowing order read or write operations. Unauthorized attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Actor identity, requested order operation, target order.
Output: Authorization decision, order operation result, audit record.
1.57 Account and Administrative Action Audit Logging
Description: The system must maintain audit logs for significant account and administrative actions, including account activation, account updates, administrator login failures, role-based permission decisions, product changes, inventory changes, order status changes, and email dispatch outcomes. Audit records should support troubleshooting, compliance review, and dispute resolution.
Input: Action type, actor identity, target record, timestamp, result.
Output: Audit record stored.

Functional Requirement
1.1 Customer Registration Function
Description: Customers can create a new account by providing personal information. The system validates the email for uniqueness and the password for strength, creates the customer account, and sends a confirmation message to the customer.
Input: Customer personal information including name, email, and password.
Output: Registered customer account and confirmation message.
1.2 Customer Login Function
Description: Registered customers can log in using their email and password. The system verifies the credentials, creates a customer session, and logs the login activity. Failed or expired authentication must not expose sensitive account or session details.
Input: Customer email and password.
Output: Logged-in customer session, homepage or dashboard display, or login failure message.
1.3 Customer Logout Function
Description: Customers can log out of their session. The system invalidates the active session, redirects the customer to the login or home page, and records the logout activity. Logout attempts should be logged regardless of whether the session was active, expired, or invalid.
Input: Customer logout request and session state.
Output: Logged-out session, redirect to login or home page, logout audit record.
1.4 Session-Based Access Control
Description: Customer actions that require account ownership, including cart operations, order placement, order history viewing, payment record retrieval, and payment information updates, must require a valid authenticated session. Requests without a valid session must be denied before protected data or transactional processing is accessed.
Input: Customer session status, protected action request, customer identity.
Output: Action allowed for authenticated owner, or access denied with a user-facing reason.
1.5 Customer Contact Information Management
Description: Customers can add, modify, or delete their contact information, such as address and phone number. Contact information used for order confirmation must be retrieved reliably. If contact information is missing, incomplete, or malformed, the system must present a recoverable error and instruct the customer to update their contact details before confirmation can be resent.
Input: Customer identifier, updated contact details, confirmation notification request.
Output: Updated contact information, contact information retrieval result, or contact update instruction.
1.6 Product Browsing Function
Description: Customers can browse products by category and view product details. The system must show only valid, available, browse-eligible products. Products that are deleted, unavailable, or out of stock must not be presented as purchasable, and product references used in browsing must correspond to existing product records.
Input: Selected category, request to view product details, product availability status.
Output: Product list or product details with current availability indicators.
1.7 Product Search Function
Description: Customers can search for products using keywords or filters such as category and price range. Search results must reflect current product details and availability, including inventory indicators, and must not return stale or ineligible product information.
Input: Search term, selected filters, product inventory availability.
Output: Search results including product name, price, image, and availability indicators.
1.8 Product Detail Availability Consistency
Description: If a product becomes unavailable after a category or search result has been displayed, the system must prevent stale product details from being shown as purchasable. The customer should receive an unavailable product indicator, and the product list should reflect the updated availability state on the next load.
Input: Product details request, product availability status, product list state.
Output: Product details display for available products or unavailable product message.
1.9 Product Category Management
Description: Administrators can create, update, and delete product categories. When a category is deleted, the system must apply defined impact rules for associated products, such as preventing deletion while products exist, reassigning products to a default category, marking products as uncategorized, or hiding affected products from customer-facing listings. Existing order history must remain interpretable after category changes.
Input: Category name, category ID, updated category details, affected product records.
Output: Created, updated, or deleted category, updated product category visibility, preserved order history interpretability.
1.10 Product Management Function
Description: Administrators can add, modify, or delete products and manage their associated category and inventory information. Changes must be reflected consistently in browsing, search, inventory checks, and order placement.
Input: Product details including name, price, category, and inventory.
Output: Updated product records, category records, and inventory records.
1.11 Inventory Management Function
Description: Administrators can manage product inventory levels, including updates and restocking alerts. Inventory data must remain consistent with browsing, cart operations, order placement, and payment outcomes.
Input: Product inventory update request from the administrator.
Output: Updated inventory levels and restocking alerts when needed.
1.12 Shopping Cart Addition Function
Description: Customers can add products to their shopping cart. If no active cart exists for the customer, the system must automatically initialize one and add the requested item in a single atomic operation. The system must verify product identity, product availability, inventory sufficiency, and requested quantity before accepting the item.
Input: Customer identity, product ID, quantity.
Output: Active shopping cart created or updated, or add-to-cart failure response.
1.13 Shopping Cart Modification Function
Description: Customers can modify quantities or remove items from their shopping cart. The system must apply cart changes atomically: either the full change succeeds or the cart remains in its previous state. The system must revalidate current inventory on quantity updates and return a clear reason if the change is rejected.
Input: Cart item modification request, requested quantity, current inventory levels.
Output: Updated shopping cart, unchanged cart with failure message, or rejected quantity update.
1.14 Shopping Cart Deletion Function
Description: Customers can clear all items from their shopping cart. The system must delete the cart contents, return a clear deletion outcome, and record the deletion event for traceability. If deletion fails, the cart must remain unchanged and the customer must receive a failure message.
Input: Customer request to delete the cart, customer identifier, cart identifier.
Output: Empty shopping cart, deletion confirmation, deletion failure message, cart deletion audit record.
1.15 Cart State Synchronization
Description: After every cart addition, modification, or deletion, the system must return the authoritative current cart state, including item list, quantities, line totals, and cart total. Order placement must use the latest persisted cart state and must not rely on stale client-side or in-memory cart data.
Input: Cart mutation request, shopping cart state.
Output: Updated cart state summary available for order placement.
1.16 Cart and Order Price Consistency
Description: Product pricing used for cart totals and order placement must be consistent. The system must capture or determine a reliable pricing basis for cart and order calculations, display any price discrepancy before payment, and ensure the final order amount matches the customer-approved amount.
Input: Product ID, selected quantity, product price, cart contents, order placement request.
Output: Consistent unit price, cart total, and order total.
1.17 Cart and Order Failure Categorization
Description: When cart modification or order placement fails, the system must categorize the reason, such as stock unavailability, invalid quantity, payment decline, session expiry, or system error. The customer must receive a specific, actionable message rather than a generic failure response.
Input: Cart modification failure or order placement failure reason.
Output: User-facing error category and recovery guidance.
1.18 Order Placement Function
Description: Customers can place an order by confirming the cart and completing checkout. The system must validate the authenticated session, latest cart state, product identities, live inventory levels, payment method ownership, and customer-approved pricing before processing payment or confirming the order.
Input: Valid shopping cart, customer session, payment method, customer confirmation.
Output: New order record, payment result, inventory update, or order placement rejection.
1.19 Order Placement Inventory Availability Precondition
Description: Before payment processing begins, the system must check live inventory levels for every item in the cart. If any item is out of stock or insufficiently stocked, order placement must be blocked and the customer must be informed of the affected items. The inventory check used for this decision must be consistent with the inventory state that will be decremented on successful order placement.
Input: Shopping cart items, current product inventory levels.
Output: Order placement allowed or blocked, item-level stock availability decision.
1.20 Payment Processing Function
Description: Customers can process payments during checkout. The system verifies payment details, confirms payment status, and updates order and inventory data only according to the final payment outcome. Payment must not be processed using a payment method that does not belong to the authenticated customer.
Input: Payment method, payment details, customer session, order details.
Output: Confirmed payment status, payment failure outcome, updated order and inventory data.
1.21 Payment Information Update Function
Description: Customers can update their stored payment information. The system must verify that the requester is the owner of the payment information before applying changes. Unauthorized update attempts must be rejected and logged.
Input: Payment information update request, requester identity, updated payment method details.
Output: Updated payment information or update denied result.
1.22 Payment Record Retrieval Access Control
Description: Payment record information associated with an order may be retrieved only by authorized customers or authorized administrators. The system verifies the requester’s identity, role, active session, and rights to the specified order before returning any payment data. Unauthorized requests must be denied without disclosing payment details.
Input: Payment record retrieval request, order identifier, requester identity and role.
Output: Payment record summary or access denied result.
1.23 Payment Status Transition Validation
Description: Payment status changes must follow defined valid transition rules. The system must reject invalid transitions, such as moving a refunded payment back to pending, and must preserve the current payment state when a requested transition is invalid.
Input: Current payment status, requested status change.
Output: Payment status transition accepted or rejected.
1.24 Order Placement Failure Rollback
Description: If order placement fails due to payment failure, payment timeout, inventory update failure, order record creation failure, or another downstream failure, the system must roll back any partial order state, release reserved inventory, and prevent duplicate orders on retry. The customer must receive a clear failure outcome and recovery instruction. Rollback operations must be idempotent and logged.
Input: Order placement attempt, payment result, inventory reservation, partial order state, failure reason.
Output: Restored order and inventory state, failure notification, rollback audit record.
1.25 Inventory Reservation Rollback
Description: If inventory has been reserved or decremented during a failed order placement attempt, the system must restore stock to the prior level or record the failure for manual resolution. Inventory rollback must be atomic and idempotent to prevent double-releasing stock or leaving phantom reservations.
Input: Inventory reservation, order placement failure, affected product identifiers and quantities.
Output: Reserved inventory released, restored inventory levels, or rollback failure record.
1.26 Order Record Finalization
Description: The order record must reflect the final placement, payment, and confirmation outcomes. If placement, payment, or confirmation fails, the order record must show the corresponding failure or pending state and must not remain in an ambiguous intermediate state. Finalization must be idempotent so retries or delayed callbacks do not create duplicate or conflicting states.
Input: Order placement outcome, payment status, order confirmation status.
Output: Created or finalized order record state.
1.27 Order Confirmation Function
Description: The system confirms orders and sends confirmation messages to customers. Confirmation content must match the latest order confirmation status, order details, and intended recipient. Confirmation must not be marked delivered if the message cannot be sent successfully.
Input: Order details, customer contact information, confirmation status.
Output: Order confirmation status update and confirmation message.
1.28 Order Confirmation Delivery Failure Handling
Description: If order confirmation delivery fails, the system must keep or restore the confirmation delivery state to pending or undelivered, log the failure, and make confirmation information available in the application where possible. The system should retry delivery according to a bounded policy and escalate unresolved failures for manual review. The business order record itself should not be rolled back solely because notification delivery failed.
Input: Confirmation delivery attempt, delivery failure event, customer contact information.
Output: Pending or undelivered confirmation state, retry or escalation outcome, delivery failure audit record.
1.29 Order Confirmation Status Transition Validation
Description: Confirmation status changes must follow a defined state model. Invalid confirmation transitions must be rejected, and confirmation status must remain unchanged. Status changes must propagate consistently to order details, order history, administrative views, and related order artifacts.
Input: Current confirmation status, requested status change, order identifier.
Output: Valid transition applied, invalid transition rejected, synchronized order representation.
1.30 Manage Order Confirmation Function
Description: Authorized administrators can modify the confirmation status of an order and send updated notifications to customers. All updates must be validated against allowed state transitions, logged, and synchronized across customer-facing and administrative order views.
Input: Administrator confirmation status change request, order identifier.
Output: Updated order confirmation status, customer notification if required, audit record.
1.31 Order History Viewing Function
Description: Registered customers can view their own previous orders and access order details. Order history access must require a valid authenticated session and must be scoped to the authenticated customer’s own orders. Unauthorized or unauthenticated requests must be denied without disclosing order details or order counts.
Input: Customer identity, order history request, customer session state.
Output: Authorized order history list or access denied result.
1.32 Order History Failure Fallback
Description: If order history cannot be retrieved, the system must provide a clear error explanation and support instruction. Fallback paths must still enforce authorization and must not disclose order details to unauthenticated or unauthorized requesters.
Input: Order history retrieval failure, customer authentication status, order details request.
Output: Final error explanation, support instruction, or denied unauthorized access.
1.33 Order History and Confirmation Status Alignment
Description: Order history must display the current confirmation and order status for each order. If confirmation or order status changes, order history and all other customer or administrative order views must reflect the updated state and must not display stale or contradictory information.
Input: Past orders, current order status, current confirmation status.
Output: Order history displaying current and consistent order details.
1.34 Order History Access Auditing
Description: Order history access events must be recorded for traceability. Each record should include the customer identity, timestamp, and scope of records accessed.
Input: Customer identity, order history access request.
Output: Immutable order history access audit record.
1.35 Manage Order Function
Description: Authorized administrators can modify or process orders, including updating status and initiating refunds. Order management actions must preserve order, payment, confirmation, and inventory consistency.
Input: Administrator order modification or processing request.
Output: Updated order status, payment status, confirmation status, or inventory state where necessary.
1.36 Inventory Recovery Notification
Description: When an order placement failure triggers inventory recovery, the system should record the recovery outcome and may notify designated administrators for operational visibility. If the notification cannot be delivered, the suppression or failure must be recorded.
Input: Order placement failure, inventory recovery outcome, administrator contact.
Output: Recovery notification outcome or recorded suppression.
1.37 Administrator Management Function
Description: Super administrators can add, modify, or deactivate other administrators. Administrator management operations must be restricted to authorized administrators only, and unauthorized attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Administrator details, actor identifier, administrator operation type.
Output: Updated administrator records or allowed/denied decision.
1.38 Administrator Operation Authorization
Description: Administrative operations, including product management, category management, inventory management, order management, payment management, plugin management, and administrator management, must require appropriate administrator authorization. Unauthorized attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Actor identifier, administrator role, requested administrative operation.
Output: Operation allowed or denied, authorization audit record.
1.39 Manage Payment Function
Description: Authorized administrators can review and modify payment records, including initiating refunds. Payment management operations must enforce access control and valid payment status transition rules.
Input: Administrator payment modification or refund request.
Output: Updated payment status, associated order records, or rejected transition.
1.40 Plugin Installation Function
Description: Authorized administrators can install plugins to extend system functionality. The system records plugin installation events for traceability.
Input: Plugin name and installation request from the administrator.
Output: Installed and activated plugin with event logged.
1.41 Plugin Configuration Function
Description: Authorized administrators can configure settings of installed plugins. Plugin configuration changes must be validated, applied only by authorized administrators, and recorded for auditability.
Input: Plugin configuration settings or update request from the administrator.
Output: Updated plugin configuration and audit record.
1.42 Plugin Uninstallation Function
Description: Authorized administrators can uninstall plugins after ensuring they are not in use. The system removes the plugin and associated configurations, records the event, and preserves relevant audit records even when configuration data is removed.
Input: Plugin ID and uninstall request from the administrator.
Output: Removed plugin and associated configuration, event log, preserved audit records.
1.43 Manage Plugin Function
Description: Authorized administrators can activate, deactivate, or remove plugins and their configurations. Plugin management actions must be logged and must not discard previously recorded operational audit events.
Input: Plugin management request from the administrator.
Output: Updated plugin status and configurations, audit event record.
1.44 Event Logging Across Core Workflows
Description: Significant user and system actions must be recorded for traceability across core workflows, including registration, login, logout, cart operations, order placement, payment processing, inventory changes, order confirmation, order history access, administrator actions, and plugin changes. Each event should include action type, actor identity, correlation key, timestamp, and outcome.
Input: Action type, actor identity, correlation key, event timestamp, action outcome.
Output: Persisted event record.

Functional Requirement
1.1 Customer Registration Function
Description: Customers can register for a new account by providing valid personal information, a valid email address, password, and optional contact information. The system validates the input, checks for duplicate accounts, creates the customer account, stores related personal and contact information, and sends a confirmation email. If registration fails before completion, partially created records must be rolled back. If only confirmation email delivery fails after account creation, the account must remain traceable and the delivery failure must be recorded for retry without creating duplicate accounts.
Input: Name, email, password, optional contact information.
Output: Customer account created, personal and contact information stored, confirmation email sent or delivery failure recorded, registration failure message when applicable.
1.2 Customer Login Function
Description: Customers can log in by entering their registered email and password. The system validates credentials, creates an authenticated customer session only after successful authentication, and records the login attempt. Failed login attempts must not create a session or display personalized content, and the customer must receive clear error feedback and be redirected to the login page or homepage.
Input: Email, password, login attempt context.
Output: Authenticated customer session and dashboard access, or login failure status with audit record and no authenticated session.
1.3 Customer Logout Function
Description: Customers can log out of the system. The system terminates or invalidates the active session, redirects the customer to the homepage or login page, and records the logout attempt. If primary session invalidation fails, the system must apply a safe fallback such as clearing client-side authentication state or forcing token expiry so the customer cannot continue as authenticated. Logout outcomes must be recorded for audit purposes.
Input: Logout request, current session identifier, customer session state.
Output: Non-authenticated session state, redirect outcome, logout audit record, fallback outcome when applicable.
1.4 Customer Session and Access Control
Description: Customer-protected actions must require a valid authenticated session belonging to the account owner. This includes personal information updates, contact information management, shopping cart actions, checkout, purchase history viewing, payment viewing, email record viewing, and order cancellation. Unauthorized or unauthenticated requests must be denied before protected data is queried or modified.
Input: Authenticated user identity, session state, requested customer operation, target customer account.
Output: Operation allowed or denied, access denied message, no data modification on denial.
1.5 Personal Information Management Function
Description: Customers can view and update their own personal information, such as name or email. Authorized administrators may manage customer personal information where permitted. The system validates submitted fields, applies updates atomically, and returns a clear update result. If the update fails, existing information must remain unchanged. If an email address is changed, pending confirmation links for the previous email should be invalidated and the new email should require verification where applicable.
Input: Customer identifier, updated personal information fields, authenticated actor identity.
Output: Updated personal information, unchanged personal information on failure, validation errors, confirmation status.
1.6 Personal Information Update Notification and Audit
Description: Successful personal information updates should generate an update status notification or confirmation email where required. Notifications must not falsely confirm updates that were rejected or not persisted. The system must record an audit trail for personal information changes, including changed fields, timestamp, actor identity, and update outcome.
Input: Personal information update result, customer identity, notification dispatch result.
Output: Update status message, confirmation email dispatch result, personal information update audit record.
1.7 Contact Information Management Function
Description: Customers can add, update, view, or delete their own contact information, such as phone number and address. The system validates required fields and formats before storage. Contact information deletion must be blocked when the information is required for active orders or pending transactions. Unauthorized changes must be denied.
Input: Customer identifier, contact information fields, contact deletion request, authenticated actor identity.
Output: Created, updated, retrieved, or deleted contact information; validation failure; access denied result.
1.8 Contact Information Validation and Failure Handling
Description: Contact information updates must be validated atomically. If any submitted field is invalid, no partial contact information may be persisted. If an update cannot be confirmed or recorded consistently, the system must preserve or roll back to the previous contact information state and return a clear failure message.
Input: Phone number, address fields, update request, update processing result.
Output: Field-level validation result, updated contact information, unchanged contact information on failure, user-facing error message.
1.9 Purchase History Viewing Function
Description: Customers can view their own purchase history, including order number, date, product names, quantities, line totals, total amount, and current order status. Purchase history access must be scoped to the authenticated customer’s own account. Attempts to access another customer’s purchase history must be denied without returning any data.
Input: Customer identity, purchase history request, session state.
Output: Authorized purchase history display or access denied response.
1.10 Purchase History Failure Handling and Logging
Description: If purchase history cannot be retrieved, the system must show a user-facing failure message instead of a silent empty state or raw error. Partial or incomplete order details must be flagged. Purchase history viewing and retrieval failures should be recorded for audit and operational monitoring.
Input: Purchase history request, retrieval result, customer identity, viewing timestamp.
Output: Purchase history display, safe error response, viewing or failure event record.
1.11 Purchase History Synchronization with Orders
Description: Purchase history must reflect current order data and status. When an order is created, updated, cancelled, or changes confirmation status, the customer’s purchase history must be updated or retrieved from authoritative order data so that stale or contradictory order information is not shown.
Input: Order data, order status change, customer identity.
Output: Purchase history updated or displayed with current order status.
1.12 Product Addition Function
Description: Authorized administrators can add new products to the system by providing product details such as name, description, price, category, and inventory quantity. The system validates all required fields, verifies that the category exists, validates price and inventory quantity constraints, and creates product, category association, and inventory records atomically.
Input: Product name, description, price, category identifier, inventory quantity, administrator identity.
Output: Product record created, category association stored, inventory initialized, or product addition rejected with validation errors.
1.13 Product Addition Failure Handling
Description: If product creation, category association, or inventory initialization fails, the system must roll back any partial product records, category links, or inventory entries. The administrator must receive a clear error message, and no incomplete product record should remain available for browsing, cart addition, checkout, or confirmation workflows.
Input: Product addition request, product creation result, category association result, inventory update result.
Output: Product addition accepted or rejected, rollback result, user-facing error message.
1.14 Product Removal Function
Description: Authorized administrators can remove products from the system only when removal will not break active purchasing activity. Before removal, the system must check for active orders, pending transactions, and active cart references. If blocking references exist, removal must be denied and the product state must remain unchanged.
Input: Product identifier, active order references, active cart references, administrator identity.
Output: Product removed, removal blocked with reason, product availability unchanged when blocked.
1.15 Product Removal Impact Handling
Description: When a product is removed or made unavailable, carts containing the affected product must be updated so the product is no longer shown as a valid purchasable item. Affected customers should be notified where appropriate. If inventory or availability updates fail during removal, the system must roll back or compensate so product and inventory states remain consistent.
Input: Removed product identifier, affected cart references, affected customer identifiers, inventory adjustment result.
Output: Updated cart display, cart impact notification, consistent product availability state, rollback or failure record.
1.16 Product Information Update Function
Description: Authorized administrators can update existing product information, including name, description, price, category, and inventory-related fields. The system validates submitted values and applies changes atomically. Failed updates must not leave product, category, or inventory data in a partial or inconsistent state.
Input: Product identifier, updated product fields, administrator identity.
Output: Updated product information or unchanged product state with failure message.
1.17 Product Price and Inventory Quantity Constraints
Description: Product prices and inventory quantities must be validated before product creation or update. Price must be a positive numeric value within configured limits. Inventory quantity must be a non-negative integer within configured limits. Invalid values must reject the operation with field-specific errors and no partial persistence.
Input: Product price value, inventory quantity value, product creation or update request.
Output: Validation result, accepted product data, or rejected operation with descriptive errors.
1.18 Product Categorization Function
Description: Authorized administrators can assign or modify product categories. The system validates the category and updates the product-category association. Category changes must be reflected in customer-facing category browsing and related product listings. Cart items must not continue to reference invalid or removed category associations.
Input: Product identifier, category identifier, category assignment request.
Output: Product categorized, category listing updated, invalid association resolved or flagged.
1.19 Category Management Function
Description: Authorized administrators can add, update, or remove product categories. The system validates category data and updates associated product relationships. Category removal must define how affected products are handled, such as blocking removal, reassigning products, marking them uncategorized, or hiding them from browsing.
Input: Category selection, category action, category details, affected product records.
Output: Category created, updated, or removed; product associations updated; category browsing state refreshed.
1.20 Inventory Management Function
Description: Authorized administrators can view and modify inventory levels for products. The system updates inventory quantities, provides current inventory visibility, and records inventory management events. Failed inventory updates must return clear errors and must not leave inventory counts inconsistent.
Input: Product identifier, inventory query request, updated inventory quantity, administrator identity.
Output: Current inventory level displayed, inventory level updated, or inventory update failure response.
1.21 Shopping Cart Addition Function
Description: Customers can add products to their shopping cart during a valid customer session. The system validates product existence, availability, category consistency, requested quantity, and current inventory before adding the item. The cart must be linked to the authenticated customer context.
Input: Customer session, product identifier, requested quantity.
Output: Product added to shopping cart, cart linked to customer, or add-to-cart rejection message.
1.22 Shopping Cart Viewing Function
Description: Customers can view the contents of their shopping cart, including product name, quantity, unit price, line total, and cart total. Cart contents must reflect the current valid cart state and must not display removed or unavailable products as purchasable.
Input: Customer session, shopping cart view request.
Output: Shopping cart summary, cart item list, total amount, invalid item indicators where applicable.
1.23 Shopping Cart Modification Function
Description: Customers can modify item quantities or remove items from their shopping cart. The system validates the cart item, requested quantity, inventory availability, and customer ownership before applying the change. Cart updates must be atomic: failed modifications must leave the cart unchanged and return a clear failure reason.
Input: Cart item selection, quantity change, remove action, customer session.
Output: Updated cart, unchanged cart on failure, modification confirmation or failure message.
1.24 Cart Item Management Function
Description: Customers can manage individual cart items by viewing details, changing quantities, or removing specific items. The system must keep CartItem data consistent with the Shopping Cart and Product records. Removed or invalid product references must be resolved, removed, or flagged before checkout.
Input: Cart item identifier, cart item action, customer session.
Output: Cart item details, updated cart item, removed cart item, or invalid cart item warning.
1.25 Checkout Function
Description: Customers can proceed to checkout using a valid authenticated session, selected shipping address, current cart items, and payment method. The system validates cart contents, inventory availability, shipping information, payment details, and customer authorization before creating an order or processing payment.
Input: Cart items, shipping address, payment method, customer session, checkout confirmation.
Output: Checkout accepted with order creation, or checkout rejected with clear reason.
1.26 Checkout Inventory Validation
Description: Checkout may proceed only when requested quantities are available in current inventory. The system must validate live inventory against cart quantities before payment processing. If any item is unavailable or insufficiently stocked, checkout must be blocked and the customer must be informed of the affected items.
Input: Cart item data, requested quantities, current inventory levels.
Output: Availability confirmed and checkout permitted, or checkout blocked with shortage message.
1.27 Order Creation from Checkout
Description: Upon successful checkout, the system creates a persistent order record and corresponding order item records from the current cart snapshot. The order must capture customer identity, selected cart items, quantities, prices, total amount, and status. The cart must be cleared or marked as checked out only after successful order creation.
Input: Checkout summary, authenticated customer account, cart items with quantities and prices.
Output: Order record created, order item records created, cart cleared or finalized.
1.28 Order Item Construction Function
Description: Order items must accurately match the customer’s selected cart items at checkout confirmation. The system preserves selected product identifiers, quantities, and prices, computes item totals, and links all order items to the created order. If any order item cannot be persisted, the order creation transaction must roll back.
Input: Selected cart items, cart quantities, product identifiers, item prices.
Output: Order items created, item totals computed, rollback on persistence failure.
1.29 Order Lifecycle Persistence and Downstream Effects
Description: After successful payment confirmation, the system must persist the order and order items, deduct purchased quantities from inventory, finalize the checked-out cart state, and mark the order confirmation email as ready for dispatch. If any downstream step fails after payment succeeds, the system must apply compensating recovery steps and flag the order for review rather than leaving data inconsistent.
Input: Checkout outcome, payment status, order items, customer identifier.
Output: Persisted order record, inventory deduction record, cart cleared state, order confirmation readiness, recovery status if needed.
1.30 Payment Processing Function
Description: The system processes the customer’s selected payment method and validates payment details. A successful payment must be stored, associated with the order, and used to determine whether the order can be finalized. Failed payments must not create confirmed orders or deduct final inventory.
Input: Payment method, payment details, order amount, customer session.
Output: Payment stored and associated with order, payment success or failure status.
1.31 Payment Viewing Function
Description: Customers and administrators can view payment details only when authorized. Customers may view payment records associated with their own orders, while administrators may view records according to their role permissions. Unauthorized requests must be denied without exposing payment data.
Input: Payment record selection, requester identity, requester role.
Output: Payment details displayed or access denied response.
1.32 Order Confirmation Email Sending Function
Description: The system sends an order confirmation email after successful order finalization. The email must use finalized order data and the customer’s current valid email address. An EmailRecord must be created for traceability and linked to the corresponding customer and order.
Input: Finalized order data, customer email address, confirmation event.
Output: Confirmation email sent, EmailRecord created, confirmation event recorded.
1.33 Order Confirmation Email Failure Handling
Description: If an order confirmation email cannot be sent or its EmailRecord cannot be retrieved, the system must record the failure and provide a customer-facing message with a recovery option such as resend request. Email delivery failure must not falsely indicate successful delivery.
Input: Order confirmation email, email delivery result, EmailRecord retrieval result.
Output: Email sent status, delivery failure record, resend option, user-facing failure message.
1.34 Email Record Management Function
Description: Authorized administrators can view, manage, or delete EmailRecord entries according to permissions. Customers may view email records related to their own account where supported. Email record access must be authorized and logged.
Input: Email record selection, email record action, requester identity.
Output: Email record displayed, updated, deleted, or access denied.
1.35 Order Cancellation Function
Description: Customers or administrators can cancel an order if it is in an eligible status. The system validates the actor’s authorization and the order’s current lifecycle state before cancellation. When cancellation succeeds, the order is marked cancelled and inventory is restored or adjusted according to fulfillment status.
Input: Order selection, cancel order action, actor identity, current order status.
Output: Order cancelled, inventory updated if applicable, cancellation denied when ineligible.
1.36 Order Item Management Function
Description: Authorized administrators can edit, remove, or update the status of items in an order where business rules permit. The system must update the order, order items, payment implications, and inventory consistently. Unauthorized or invalid changes must be rejected.
Input: Order item selection, requested change, administrator identity.
Output: Updated order item, updated order and inventory state, or rejection message.
1.37 Product Management Authorization
Description: Product catalog operations, including product addition, removal, update, categorization, and inventory management, must be restricted to authorized administrators. The system must check role permissions before executing catalog mutations. Unauthorized attempts must be denied and recorded.
Input: Actor identity, actor role, product operation request.
Output: Product operation allowed or denied, authorization audit record.
1.38 Administrator Management Function
Description: Authorized administrators can manage administrator accounts by updating, deactivating, or managing permitted administrator details. The system must validate permissions before administrator account changes and record management events.
Input: Administrator account selection, management action, requesting administrator identity.
Output: Administrator account updated or deactivated, or access denied response.
1.39 Customer Management Function
Description: Authorized administrators can manage customer accounts, including updating customer information or deactivating accounts where permitted. The system must validate administrator authorization and preserve account data consistency.
Input: Customer account selection, management action, administrator identity.
Output: Customer account updated, deactivated, or management request denied.
1.40 Personal and Contact Information Query Function
Description: Customers and authorized administrators can retrieve stored personal and contact information records. Customers may retrieve only their own records. Unauthorized retrieval attempts must be denied and logged.
Input: Customer identity, requester identity, query request.
Output: Personal and contact information displayed or access denied response.
1.41 Plugin Installation Function
Description: Authorized administrators can install plugins to expand system functionality. The system validates the plugin before activation, stores plugin information, updates the interface or system behavior as applicable, and records the installation event.
Input: Plugin details or file, administrator identity.
Output: Plugin installed and activated, or installation rejected with reason.
1.42 Plugin Configuration Function
Description: Authorized administrators can configure installed plugins. The system validates configuration settings, applies valid changes, and records configuration events. Invalid configuration must be rejected without leaving plugin settings partially updated.
Input: Plugin configuration settings, administrator identity.
Output: Updated plugin configuration or validation failure message.
1.43 User Interface Specification Management Function
Description: Authorized administrators can manage user interface specifications and check interface compliance against defined requirements. The system applies approved specification changes and can generate compliance reports identifying non-compliant interface elements.
Input: UI specification update, compliance check request, administrator identity.
Output: Updated UI specification, compliance report, highlighted non-compliant elements.
1.44 Event Logging and Audit Recovery
Description: Significant actions must be recorded for traceability, including registration, login, logout, personal information updates, contact information updates, product changes, cart operations, checkout, payment processing, order creation, order cancellation, purchase history viewing, email delivery, and administrator actions. If event logging fails after a successful primary operation, the primary operation should remain valid while the logging failure is captured internally for remediation.
Input: Operation context, actor identity, affected entity identifiers, primary operation outcome, logging result.
Output: Audit record stored, or internal logging failure record with primary operation outcome preserved.
1.45 Purchase History Archival and Deletion Control
Description: Authorized actors may request archival or deletion of purchase history records according to retention rules and applicable data rights. The system validates authorization and retention policy before archiving or deleting records. Archived records must be hidden from standard purchase history views but recoverable by authorized administrators where permitted.
Input: Customer identity, retention request, requester identity.
Output: Purchase history archival status, deletion status, or request denial.

Functional Requirement
Functional Requirements
All functional requirements are written in active voice, concise, unambiguous, and verifiable.
FR-001
Requirement Description: The system shall allow users to create an account by providing valid personal information. The system shall validate required fields, email format, email uniqueness, password rules, and password confirmation before creating the account.
Input: Name, Email, Password, Confirm Password
Output: Account created with default access level, or validation error message.
FR-002
Requirement Description: The system shall prevent partial account creation when registration fails. If account creation fails due to invalid input, duplicate email, password mismatch, missing required fields, or system error, the system shall not persist a partial account record.
Input: Account creation request, validation result, creation outcome
Output: Account creation rejected with clear failure reason; no partial account record created.
FR-003
Requirement Description: The system shall create an audit record for each account creation attempt. The audit record shall include the account identity, timestamp, and outcome of the registration attempt.
Input: Account identity, creation request outcome
Output: Immutable account creation audit record.
FR-004
Requirement Description: The system shall authenticate users during login using their registered email and password. The system shall create an authenticated session only when credentials are valid.
Input: Email, Password
Output: Login success with authenticated session, or login failure message.
FR-005
Requirement Description: The system shall handle failed login attempts safely. Failed authentication shall not create a session, shall not display protected content, and shall return a consistent non-revealing error message.
Input: Email, Password, authentication attempt outcome
Output: Login failure response; no authenticated session created.
FR-006
Requirement Description: The system shall apply configurable retry restrictions after repeated failed login attempts. The system shall track failure counts server-side and apply lockout or progressive delay after the configured threshold is exceeded.
Input: Account identity, authentication attempt outcome, cumulative failure count
Output: Retry restriction applied when threshold is exceeded; lockout event logged.
FR-007
Requirement Description: The system shall bind each authenticated session to the verified account identity. All subsequent protected requests shall use this session identity to determine the user’s permissions and owned resources.
Input: Account identifier, authentication outcome
Output: Authenticated session bound to verified account identity.
FR-008
Requirement Description: The system shall enable users to log out securely. When logout succeeds, the system shall terminate the session and prevent further authenticated actions using that session.
Input: Logout request, session identifier
Output: Session terminated.
FR-009
Requirement Description: The system shall handle logout failures safely. If normal logout processing fails, the system shall apply a fallback mechanism such as server-side invalidation, token expiry, or clearing authentication cookies so the user cannot continue operating as authenticated.
Input: Logout request, session state, logout outcome
Output: Session termination confirmed, or clear error message with safe fallback outcome.
FR-010
Requirement Description: The system shall record session termination events. Each record shall include the account identity, session identifier, termination reason, and timestamp.
Input: Account identity, session identifier, termination reason
Output: Immutable session termination audit record.
FR-011
Requirement Description: The system shall restrict user profile changes to the account owner. The system shall verify the authenticated session identity before applying profile updates.
Input: Account identity, requested profile changes, authenticated session identity
Output: Authorized profile update or access denied response.
FR-012
Requirement Description: The system shall allow users to view a list of available products categorized by type. Product listings shall include images, prices, and descriptions.
Input: Product catalog request, category selection
Output: Displayed product list with images, prices, and descriptions.
FR-013
Requirement Description: The system shall provide a fallback response when product catalog data is unavailable. If live catalog data cannot be retrieved, the system may display cached product data within an acceptable staleness threshold; otherwise, it shall display a clear empty-state or retry message.
Input: Product catalog request, product data availability status, cached product data
Output: Product list displayed, cached product list displayed, or catalog unavailable message.
FR-014
Requirement Description: The system shall display categories only when they correspond to available and correctly classified products. If category data cannot be retrieved, the system shall still allow browsing through an unfiltered product list where possible.
Input: Product category data, product availability status
Output: Category-filtered product list, unfiltered product list, or category unavailable message.
FR-015
Requirement Description: The system shall prevent users from adding products to the cart when required product data is unavailable or incomplete.
Input: Product ID, Quantity, product data availability status
Output: Add-to-cart denied with product data unavailable message.
FR-016
Requirement Description: The system shall allow users to add selected products to their shopping cart. The system shall validate product identity, availability, and requested quantity before updating the cart.
Input: Product ID, Quantity, user session
Output: Updated cart contents or add-to-cart validation error.
FR-017
Requirement Description: The system shall enforce valid quantity constraints for cart additions and updates. Quantities shall be positive integers and shall not exceed available stock.
Input: Product ID, Quantity, available stock
Output: Updated cart contents, or validation error message.
FR-018
Requirement Description: The system shall bind shopping cart state to the active authenticated user session. Cart contents shall not be mixed across users or sessions.
Input: User session token, cart contents, session identifier
Output: Cart contents correctly associated with active user session.
FR-019
Requirement Description: The system shall reconcile persisted cart state when a user session is restored. The system shall apply a defined reconciliation policy and display the resulting valid cart state.
Input: User session token, persisted cart state, current cart state
Output: Reconciled cart contents displayed to user.
FR-020
Requirement Description: The system shall display the total quantity and cost of items in the shopping cart. Cart totals shall reflect the latest confirmed server-side cart state.
Input: Cart contents
Output: Cart summary displayed with total quantity and total cost.
FR-021
Requirement Description: The system shall provide a meaningful cart error message when cart state cannot be retrieved or computed. The system shall not silently display blank, stale, or incorrect totals.
Input: Cart state availability
Output: Cart summary displayed or cart error message shown.
FR-022
Requirement Description: The system shall allow users to modify item quantities or remove items from the shopping cart. The system shall validate the cart state, product ID, requested quantity, and removal command before applying the change.
Input: Product ID, New Quantity, Remove Command, cart state
Output: Updated cart contents or validation error message.
FR-023
Requirement Description: The system shall preserve cart state when a cart update fails. Failed add, modify, or remove operations shall not apply partial changes and shall return a clear error message.
Input: Cart update command, update execution result
Output: Cart state preserved with cart update failure message.
FR-024
Requirement Description: The system shall display a fallback cart update failure message if the primary cart error response mechanism fails.
Input: Cart update command, cart update error handling result
Output: Generic cart update failure message.
FR-025
Requirement Description: The system shall update cart contents when product inventory or catalog data changes. If a product is removed, its price changes, or its stock becomes insufficient, the cart shall reflect the latest valid product state and notify the user of affected items.
Input: Product update event, current shopping cart state
Output: Updated cart reflecting product availability and pricing; user notification.
FR-026
Requirement Description: The system shall capture product data needed for cart and checkout consistency. Product name, price, and description used for checkout shall remain consistent with the customer-approved cart state.
Input: Product data, shopping cart contents
Output: Product data snapshot or checkout validation result.
FR-027
Requirement Description: The system shall block checkout when product data required for the transaction is unavailable or inconsistent with the approved cart state.
Input: Product data availability status, cart contents, checkout request
Output: Checkout blocked with product data error message.
FR-028
Requirement Description: The system shall process checkout by collecting shipping and payment details. The system shall validate all mandatory checkout inputs before payment processing.
Input: Shipping Address, Payment Method, Card Details, cart contents
Output: Checkout accepted or validation error message.
FR-029
Requirement Description: The system shall validate that the shopping cart contains at least one purchasable item before checkout proceeds. This validation shall occur before collecting or processing payment details.
Input: Shopping cart contents, user session
Output: Checkout permitted or checkout blocked message.
FR-030
Requirement Description: The system shall preserve the customer’s cart and entered shipping information when checkout fails. The user shall be able to correct errors and retry without re-adding items.
Input: Checkout processing result, cart state, shipping details
Output: Checkout failure message; cart state and shipping details preserved.
FR-031
Requirement Description: The system shall roll back checkout state when payment, shipping validation, order creation, or inventory reservation fails. The system shall ensure no partial order is committed and no charge is applied unless the transaction fully succeeds.
Input: Checkout request, payment result, shipping validation result, order creation result
Output: Fully committed order on success, or fully rolled-back state on failure.
FR-032
Requirement Description: The system shall use idempotency controls for payment processor calls and checkout retries to prevent duplicate charges or duplicate orders.
Input: Checkout attempt, payment request, retry request
Output: Duplicate charge or duplicate order prevented.
FR-033
Requirement Description: The system shall provide a clear checkout failure message with a definitive transaction status. The message shall identify the failure reason where possible and provide actionable next steps.
Input: Checkout processing result, transaction status
Output: Failed transaction status and recovery guidance.
FR-034
Requirement Description: The system shall notify the customer when checkout cannot complete due to payment failure. The system shall not issue an order confirmation for failed checkout.
Input: Customer Email, payment failure reason, attempted checkout details
Output: Payment failure notification or on-screen failure message.
FR-035
Requirement Description: The system shall ensure checkout-to-order consistency. If checkout succeeds, the system shall create a confirmed order linked to the successful payment; if checkout fails, no orphaned order record shall remain.
Input: Cart contents, payment result, shipping details, order creation outcome
Output: Confirmed order with payment, or rolled-back state with no partial order.
FR-036
Requirement Description: The system shall log checkout failures, rollback outcomes, and reconciliation events with sufficient detail to support investigation.
Input: Checkout attempt ID, failure stage, error reason, rollback outcome
Output: Checkout failure and rollback audit record.
FR-037
Requirement Description: The system shall send an order confirmation email only after a transaction has completed successfully and the order ID is linked to the completed transaction.
Input: Order ID, Customer Email, successful transaction confirmation
Output: Order confirmation email sent with order details.
FR-038
Requirement Description: The system shall record order confirmation email delivery attempts. Each record shall include the order ID, customer email, timestamp, delivery status, and error details when applicable.
Input: Order ID, Customer Email, email delivery outcome
Output: Email delivery attempt record.
FR-039
Requirement Description: The system shall handle order confirmation email delivery failures with a defined recovery process. The system shall retry delivery according to a defined policy and shall log unresolved failures for administrator follow-up.
Input: Email delivery outcome, Order ID, Customer Email
Output: Retry outcome, fallback notification, or failure logged.
FR-040
Requirement Description: The system shall provide an alternative way for the customer to access order confirmation details when email delivery fails. The alternative may include an in-application order status page, on-screen confirmation, or resend mechanism.
Input: Order ID, Customer Email, delivery failure status
Output: Delivery failure guidance and alternative access to order confirmation details.
FR-041
Requirement Description: The system shall allow customers to view their past orders. Order history shall be scoped strictly to the authenticated customer’s own orders and shall prevent cross-customer access.
Input: Authenticated customer identity, optional filter criteria
Output: Paginated list of prior orders belonging to the authenticated customer.
FR-042
Requirement Description: The system shall support filtering order history by date range and order status. Results shall display in reverse-chronological order by default.
Input: Customer identity, date range, order status
Output: Filtered order history list.
FR-043
Requirement Description: The system shall allow administrators to manage product inventory, including adding, editing, and removing products. Inventory changes shall update the product catalog after successful completion.
Input: Product Data, operation type
Output: Updated product catalog.
FR-044
Requirement Description: The system shall restrict product inventory management to authorized administrator accounts. Authorization checks shall be enforced server-side before any inventory or catalog change is applied.
Input: Account identity, role, inventory operation request
Output: Authorized inventory update or access denied message.
FR-045
Requirement Description: The system shall log product inventory authorization outcomes. The log shall include the account identity, attempted command, authorization result, and timestamp.
Input: Account identity, inventory operation requested, authorization result
Output: Inventory authorization audit record.
FR-046
Requirement Description: The system shall preserve catalog integrity when inventory or product update operations fail. Failed add, edit, or remove operations shall leave the catalog in its prior consistent state and return a clear failure message.
Input: Product Data, update command, update execution result
Output: Catalog update success confirmation or failure message with catalog unchanged.
FR-047
Requirement Description: The system shall provide administrators with immediate feedback for product inventory operations. The feedback shall identify the operation, affected product, success status, and corrective guidance when applicable.
Input: Product Data, operation type, operation result
Output: Administrator success or failure message.
FR-048
Requirement Description: The system shall create an immutable audit record for each product inventory change. Each record shall include the administrator identity, operation type, affected product, before and after values where applicable, and timestamp.
Input: Product Data, operation type, administrator identity
Output: Product catalog change audit record.
FR-049
Requirement Description: The system shall reflect successful inventory and product catalog changes in customer-facing product listings within a defined consistency window.
Input: Updated product catalog
Output: Updated product list with current product data.
FR-050
